弘治三年進士登科錄

玉音

弘治三年三月十二日，禮部尚書臣耿裕等於奉天門奏：「為科舉事，會試天下舉人，取中三百名。本年三月十五日殿試，合請讀卷官及執事等官，少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士劉吉等五十三員。其進士出身等第，恭依太祖高皇帝欽定資格：第一甲例取三名，第一名從六品，第二、第三名正七品，賜進士及第；第二甲從七品，賜進士出身；第三甲正八品，賜同進士出身。」奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

讀卷官

光祿大夫、柱國、少傅兼太子太師、吏部尚書、謹身殿大學士劉吉〔戊辰進士〕。
榮祿大夫、太子太保、吏部尚書王恕〔戊辰進士〕。
資善大夫、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士徐溥〔甲戌進士〕。
資善大夫、戶部尚書李敏〔甲戌進士〕。
translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates (jinshi) of the Third Year of Hongzhi (1490)

Imperial Pronouncement

On the twelfth day of the third month of the third year of Hongzhi, your servant Geng Yu, Minister of Rites, and others submitted the following memorial at Fengtian Gate: “Concerning the civil-service examinations: in the Metropolitan Examination of provincial graduates (juren) from throughout the realm, three hundred candidates have been selected. For the Palace Examination on the fifteenth day of the third month of this year, we request the appointment of fifty-three officials as examination paper readers and other officiating personnel, including Liu Ji, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. The grades of jinshi status are to follow respectfully the qualifications imperially established by Emperor Taizu Gao. In the first class, three candidates are customarily selected: the first receives rank 6b, and the second and third receive rank 7a; they are granted the distinction of ‘jinshi with honors.’ Those in the second class receive rank 7b and are granted ‘jinshi status.’ Those in the third class receive rank 8a and are granted ‘status equivalent to jinshi.’” The imperial rescript was received: “Approved.” Respectfully received.

Examination Paper Readers

Liu Ji, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor, concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year (1448).〕

Wang Shu, Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and Minister of Personnel. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year (1448).〕

Xu Pu, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, Minister of Rites, concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year (1454).〕

Li Min, Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Minister of Revenue. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year (1454).〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the third year of Hongzhi (1490), the tribute scholars went to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, all civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the Embroidered-uniform Guard set out the imperial ceremonial regalia on the vermilion steps and in the vermilion courtyard. The emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall, and officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow proclamation of examination results, led by drums and music, out through the Left Chang'an Gate. After it had been posted outside the gate, officials of Shuntian Prefecture escorted the first-place graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with ceremonial parasols, canopies, and attendants.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
…An imperial banquet was bestowed at the Ministry of Rites. After the banquet, the graduates went to the Court of State Ceremonial to rehearse the ceremonies.
On the twentieth day of the third month, the top graduate was granted court robes, a cap, and a girdle, and the metropolitan graduates (jinshi) were granted paper currency.
On the twenty-first day of the third month, the top graduate led the other metropolitan graduates in submitting a memorial expressing gratitude for imperial favor.
On the twenty-second day of the third month, the top graduate led the other metropolitan graduates to the temple of Confucius, the First Teacher, to perform the vegetable-offering rite (shicai).
The Ministry of Rites submitted a request, and the Ministry of Works was ordered to erect a stone stele at the Directorate of Education inscribed with the graduates’ names.

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted metropolitan graduate status with honors (jinshi jidi).

Qian Fu 錢福 was registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuqian, and he was second in birth order, aged thirty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Chang, and his father Zhong, a department Vice Prefect; his mother was née Lu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tang and his younger brother Zuo. His wife was née Gu. He placed ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cunye 劉存業 was registered in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, in a salt-producing household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Keda, and he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shisun, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Wen; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His wife was née Wei. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Gui 靳貴 was registered in Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, in a civilian household. A county government school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chongdao, and he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Rong, and his father Yu, a prefectural Registrar; his mother was née Fan. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His wife was née Wang. He placed first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second class: ninety men, granted metropolitan graduate (jinshi) status.

Yang Dan, registered in Jian’an County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jinshu; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was Junior Preceptor, Minister of Works, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall; he was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor and the name Wenmin. His grandfather was Xi, his father was Shiyi, and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Hong, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chaowen; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongke, his grandfather was Qi, his father was Jing, and his mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Yi, Hui, Chun, and Xuan. He married a woman née Zang. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ze, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Gongpu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenqing, his grandfather was Shuang, a county magistrate, and his father was Jian. His father’s former wife was née Shen, and his mother was née Song. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Gao. He placed fifty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

唐貴〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字用思，行一，年四十三，五月十六日生〕。曾祖汝文，祖伯誠〔贈大理寺左寺副〕，父衍，前母左氏，母徐氏。慈侍下，弟世顯、世美、世寧，娶周氏。應天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第三名。

張天爵〔貫直隸松江府華亭縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字良貴，行二，年三十四，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖真，祖壅，父佐，母徐氏。嚴侍下，兄天錫，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第五十六名，會試第四十四名。

李昆〔貫山東萊州府膠州高密縣軍籍，縣學增廣生，治禮記，字承裕，行一，年二十，四月十八日生〕。曾祖遜〔布政司理問〕，祖傑〔教授，贈都察院右僉都御史〕，父介〔都察院右僉都御史〕，母杜氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，兄杲、昂〔陰陽訓術〕、旦、昊，弟昺、冕、昇、昪，娶昝氏。山東鄉試第五十八名，會試第一百三十二名。
translation_en:
Peng Jie 彭杰, registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingjun; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-three, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Buhui; his grandfather, Rubi, was a county school instructor who received the honorary title of Hanlin Academy Compiler; and his father was Zhan. His father’s former wife was née Kuang, his mother was née Lin, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ji; his younger brothers were Huan (a jinshi of the same examination cohort), Fei, Mao, Cai, Zuo [?], and Lai [?]. His wife was née Yuan. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Gui 唐貴, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yongsi; he ranked first in his family and was aged forty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruwen; his grandfather, Bocheng, was posthumously awarded the title of Left Assistant Judge of the Court of Judicial Review; and his father was Yan. His father’s former wife was née Zuo, and his mother was née Xu. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Shixian, Shimei, and Shining. His wife was née Zhou. He placed thirty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Tianjue 張天爵, registered in a civilian household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Lianggui; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Yong, and his father Zuo; his mother was née Xu. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Tianxi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed fifty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Kun 李昆, registered in a military household in Gaomi County, Jiaozhou Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an added-quota student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Chengyu; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Xun, was a Judicial Officer in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather, Jie, was a prefectural school instructor posthumously awarded the title of Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate; and his father, Jie, was Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Du, held the title Lady of Suitability. Grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Gao, Ang (an Instructor in a School of Yin-yang Studies), Dan, and Hao; his younger brothers were Bing, Mian, Sheng, and Bian. His wife was née Zan. He placed fifty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

王瑩〔貫直隸淮安府山陽縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字汝潔，行一，年四十，九月十九日生〕。曾祖文，祖浩〔知縣〕，父穟，母張氏。具慶下，弟琰、瓛、勞，娶周氏。應天府鄉試第一百二十五名，會試第二百五十九名。

周統〔貫江西吉安府廬陵縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字伯承，行一，年三十六，六月二十九日生〕。曾祖子遜，祖詢〔教諭，贈主事〕，父孟中〔按察司副使〕，母劉氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，弟仲敞，娶陳氏。江西鄉試第八十二名，會試第二百五十八名。
translation_en:
Ning Ju, registered in Xincheng County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weichen. He ranked first in family order and was thirty-two years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was You, his grandfather Yunxian, and his father Jian; his mother was née Yang. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Xue. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shizhong, registered in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Maozhen. He ranked thirty-eighth in family order and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jibin, his grandfather Ruoqing, and his father Zhengfu; his mother was née Wang, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, Ji, Heng, and Huan; his younger brothers were Le and Shiying. He married a woman née Quan. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ying, registered in Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Rujie. He ranked first in family order and was forty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wen, his grandfather Hao〔District Magistrate〕, and his father Sui; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yan, Huan, and Lao. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Tong, registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bocheng. He ranked first in family order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zixun, his grandfather Xun〔Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary〕, and his father Mengzhong〔Surveillance Vice Commissioner〕; his mother was née Liu〔granted the title of Lady of Peace〕. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhongchang [?]. He married a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 258th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ding Pei, registered in a military household of Lu’an Guard in Zhili and a native of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Dayong; he ranked second in family order and was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yigong, his grandfather Xing, and his father Wen; his mother was née Yang and his stepmother née Feng. His father was living, and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Yu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xu, registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongli; he ranked twenty-sixth in family order and was thirty-five years old, born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Derong, his grandfather Minrang, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Yang. His father was living, and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Tai, Shun (Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission), Xiang, and Dan; his younger brothers were Xue and Xiao. He married a woman née Yu. He placed forty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Zhang, registered in an official household of Suzhou Guard in Zhili and a native of Runing Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Risheng; he ranked third in family order and was forty-five years old, born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin, a Company Commander; his grandfather was Xin, posthumously granted the title of Guard Disciplinary Officer; and his father was Jinghui, a Guard Disciplinary Officer. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title of Grand Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yao and Ming, both Battalion Commanders. He married a woman née Tang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Mian, registered in a military household of Yunnan Central Guard in Yunnan and a native of Kunshan County, Zhili, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenyong; he ranked first in family order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang, his grandfather Tong, and his father Yin; his mother was née Ding. His father was living, and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Zhang, an Investigating Censor; his younger brothers were Bing and Kun. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventeenth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Huang Xiu, registered in the strongman service of the Standard Bearer Guard and a native of Qingjiang County, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenqing; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twentieth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiheng, his grandfather Dongyi, his father Neng, and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin. He married a woman née Wen and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked 117th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengzu, registered in a civilian household in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Jizong; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the thirtieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Qingfu was granted the title of Deputy Office Chief in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; his grandfather Rui was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; his father Geng was Director of Music at the Temple of Confucius; and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Kong. He ranked fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shou, registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xuezhi; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziming; his grandfather Ne was a prefectural Registrar; his father Jin was a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née You. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Ying, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Gang. He married a woman née He. He ranked thirty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Shu, registered in a military household in Boxing County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Gongzhi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junxian, his grandfather Lai, his father Kexiang, and his mother née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Ji. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked fifty-first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

羅榮〔貫福建福州府古田縣民籍，縣學生，治易經，字志仁，行一，年二十四，十一月初一日生〕。曾祖恩〔知縣〕，祖祺，父宗蔭，母林氏。重慶下，弟謙，娶林氏。福建鄉試第八十一名，會試第二百九十八名。

崔儀〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，儒士，治詩經，字虞鳳，行五，年三十三，八月初七日生〕。曾祖建，祖永泰，父邦爵，母陳氏，繼母陳氏、翁氏。重慶下，兄鸑、順，弟麒、麟、仁、篪、𤇍、命、佑，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第二名，會試第十六名。

吳綱〔貫福建邵武府建寧縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宏舉，行五，年四十一，六月十一日生〕。曾祖必昌，祖文通，父孟禎，母袁氏，繼母徐氏。具慶下，兄自學、自昇、自輝、自寬，弟自興、自重，娶朱氏。福建鄉試第十二名，會試第二百四十九名。

仲本〔貫太醫院醫籍，直隸寶應縣人，醫官生，治易經，字與立，行四，年二十七，十一月十四日生〕。曾祖恭，祖旺〔贈尚寶司丞〕，父蘭〔太醫院院使〕，母楊氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，兄森、楷〔監生〕、檳，弟槩、榘〔禮部主事〕、相、桂、機、模、采、柯，娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第二百七十二名。
translation_en:
Luo Rong 羅榮, courtesy name Zhiren, was registered in a civilian household in Gutian County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was En, a county magistrate; his grandfather was Qi; his father was Zongyin; and his mother was née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Qian, and his wife was née Lin. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cui Yi 崔儀, courtesy name Yufeng, was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather was Yongtai; his father was Bangjue; his mother was née Chen; and his stepmothers were née Chen and née Weng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Yue and Shun; his younger brothers were Qi, Lin, Ren, Chi, 𤇍 [?], Ming, and You. His wife was née Chen. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Gang 吳綱, courtesy name Hongju, was registered in a civilian household in Jianning County, Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bichang; his grandfather was Wentong; his father was Mengzhen; his mother was née Yuan; and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zixue, Zisheng, Zihui, and Zikuan; his younger brothers were Zixing and Zizhong. His wife was née Zhu. He placed twelfth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 249th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Ben 仲本, courtesy name Yuli, was registered in a medical household attached to the Imperial Medical Academy and was a native of Baoying County in Zhili. A medical student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gong; his grandfather was Wang, posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Office of Imperial Seals; his father was Lan, Director of the Imperial Medical Academy; and his mother was née Yang, granted the title Lady of Suitability. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Sen, Kai (a student of the Directorate of Education), and Bin; his younger brothers were Gai, Ju (a secretary in the Ministry of Rites), Xiang, Gui, Ji, Mo, Cai, and Ke. His wife was née Zhao. He placed 114th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Zhong, courtesy name Daben, was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Changshu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingyuan, his grandfather Ding, his father Hong, and his mother née Zou. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zheng, and his wife was née Wan. He ranked twelfth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Anfu, courtesy name Rumian, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the seventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyu; his grandfather, Yongli, was posthumously honored as Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father was Zhen, his father's principal wife was née Zhao, and his birth mother was née Jin. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother, Yinfu, was a School Instructor; his younger brothers were Shenfu and Pingfu. His wife was née Xu. He ranked thirteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Long Kui, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in a civilian household in Yichun County, Yuanzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the eighth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qing; his grandfather, Ying, was a Clerk in a Superintendency and was honored with the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites. His father, Xian, was Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. His mother, née Zhang, was posthumously honored as Lady of Respect (gongren), and his stepmother was née Wang. His father and stepmother were both living. His younger brothers were Ce, Xia, Ai, Nao, and Jun; his wife was née Fan. He ranked sixty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Rui, courtesy name Shiqi, was registered in a military household in Qianwei County, Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhigao, his grandfather Yu, his father Yongfu, and his mother née Yi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Zhang, and his wife was née Han. He ranked sixty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
胡易〔貫江西贛州府寧都縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字光貞，行五，年三十八，八月二十九日生〕。曾祖源廣，祖伯厚，父大忠，母李氏，繼母葉氏。具慶下，兄光啓、光泰、光榮、光顯，弟光序、昺、春、晏，娶劉氏。江西鄉試第九十四名，會試第二十八名。

方良永〔貫福建興化府莆田縣，民籍，縣學增廣生，治書經，字壽卿，行一，年三十，九月十五日生〕。曾祖孟章，祖象輝，父朝深，母陳氏。重慶下，弟良節〔同科進士〕、良盛、良材，娶陳氏。福建鄉試第四十六名，會試第一百二十三名。

劉紳〔貫河南汝寧府汝陽縣，民籍，國子生，治禮記，字美用，行二，年四十三，四月初七日生〕。曾祖信，祖原〔冠帶例〕，父瑛〔布政司照磨〕，母翟氏。永感下，兄紀〔驛丞〕，弟鎧、紋，娶趙氏，繼娶吳氏。河南鄉試第一名，會試第二百四十八名。

胡儀〔貫浙江紹興府山陰縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字士望，行五十，年二十七，十二月初六日生〕。曾祖尚廉，祖珙，父錫〔義官〕，母張氏，繼母莫氏。具慶下，兄倫、倜、伉、𣉮、佶，娶宋氏。浙江鄉試第十一名，會試第二百名。
translation_en:
Hu Yi, courtesy name Guangzhen, was registered in Ningdu County, Ganzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yuanguang; his grandfather, Bohou; and his father, Dazhong. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guangqi, Guangtai, Guangrong, and Guangxian; his younger brothers were Guangxu, Bing, Chun, and Yan. His wife was née Liu. He placed ninety-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Liangyong, courtesy name Shouqing, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Mengzhang; his grandfather, Xianghui; and his father, Chaoshen. His mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Liangjie (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Liangsheng, and Liangcai. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 123rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Shen, courtesy name Meiyong, was registered in Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the seventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Yuan (entitled under the regulations to wear official cap and belt); and his father, Ying (a Records Keeper in the Provincial Administration Commission). His mother was née Zhai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Ji (a Station Master), and his younger brothers were Kai and Wen. His wife was née Zhao; his subsequent wife was née Wu. He placed first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yi, courtesy name Shiwang, was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fiftieth in the sibling order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shanglian; his grandfather, Gong; and his father, Xi (an honorary official recognized for charitable contributions). His mother was née Zhang, and his stepmother née Mo. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun, Ti, Kang, 𣉮 [?], and Ji. His wife was née Song. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
徐逵〔貫湖廣儀衞司官籍，直隸山陽縣人，國子生，治詩經，字大亨，行一，年二十九，十月初二日生〕。曾祖希賢，祖昂，父鎬〔義官〕，母管氏。具慶下，兄達，弟迪、道、暹、逺、遵，娶王氏。湖廣鄉試第二十一名，會試第三十八名。

張約〔貫直隸蘇州府長洲縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字守之，行一，年三十五，三月二十一日生〕。曾祖文淵，祖樞〔贈南京刑部郎中〕，父翥〔雲南按察使〕，母吳氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，弟蒙、貞，娶浦氏，繼娶錢氏。應天府鄉試第一百四名，會試第一百二十二名。

張定〔貫錦衣衞官籍，福建同安縣人，國子生，治書經，字子靜，行一，年二十五，八月初六日生〕。曾祖益初〔贈南京通政使〕，祖太常〔贈錦衣衞中𫠊千戶〕，父苗〔南京通政使〕，母楊氏〔封淑人〕。重慶下，弟宜、寧，娶田氏。順天府鄉試第六十二名，會試第七十五名。

韓智〔貫山東兖州府滋陽縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字愚夫，行一，年三十四，四月二十八日生〕。曾祖景華，祖晟，父惠〔知事〕，母程氏。具慶下，弟普〔知縣〕、曆，娶許氏。山東鄉試第十八名，會試第一百三名。
translation_en:
Xu Kui, courtesy name Daheng, was on the official register of the Huguang Ceremonial Guard Office and was a native of Shanyang County in the Metropolitan Region; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xixian, his grandfather Ang, his father Gao (an honorary official), and his mother née Guan; both parents were living, his elder brother was Da, his younger brothers were Di, Dao, Xian, Yuan, and Zun, and his wife was née Wang; he placed twenty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yue, courtesy name Shouzhi, was on the military register of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenyuan, his grandfather Shu (posthumously appointed Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice), his father Zhu (Yunnan Surveillance Commissioner), and his mother née Wu (enfeoffed as Lady of Suitability); his parents and grandparents were living, his younger brothers were Meng and Zhen, and he married a woman née Pu and subsequently a woman née Qian; he placed 104th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Ding, courtesy name Zijing, was on the official register of the Embroidered Uniform Guard and was a native of Tong'an County, Fujian; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yichu (posthumously appointed Nanjing Transmission Commissioner), his grandfather Taichang (posthumously appointed Battalion Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, with an unclear designation, 中𫠊 [?]), his father Miao (Nanjing Transmission Commissioner), and his mother née Yang (enfeoffed as Lady of Chastity); his parents and grandparents were living, his younger brothers were Yi and Ning, and his wife was née Tian; he placed sixty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Zhi, courtesy name Yufu, was on the civilian register of Ziyang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong; an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghua, his grandfather Sheng, his father Hui (an Administrative Clerk), and his mother née Cheng; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Pu (a District Magistrate) and Li, and his wife was née Xu; he placed eighteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
胡拱〔貫南京府軍左衛官籍，國子生，治書經，字惟辰，行一，年二十六，三月二十九日生〕。曾祖灝〔指揮僉事〕，祖寬〔都指揮僉事〕，父英，母陳氏。具慶下，娶朱氏。應天府鄉試第七十七名，會試第五十一名。

徐木〔貫河南開封府杞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字惟喬，行三，年三十，二月十五日生〕。曾祖景昇〔義官〕，祖政〔文思院副使，封主事〕，父紳〔知府〕，母李氏〔封安人〕。永感下，兄本、朱，弟材，娶李氏。河南鄉試第二名，會試第一百九十七名。

晁必登〔貫四川馬湖府平夷長官司民籍，宜賓縣人，國子生，治易經，字汝吉，行二，年二十九，三月十九日生〕。曾祖琰，祖有問〔贈戶部員外郎〕，父常〔布政司右參政〕，母劉氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄必豐，弟必第，娶田氏。四川鄉試第十五名，會試第一百一名。

何宗理〔貫陝西平凉府涇州民籍，州學增廣生，治詩經，字邦治，行一，年三十，十月二十日生〕。曾祖寧〔贈知府〕，祖源〔知府〕，父正〔知縣〕，母劉氏，繼母劉氏、薛氏。具慶下，弟宗性、宗本、宗先、宗儒，娶韓氏。陝西鄉試第六名，會試第二百三十二名。
translation_en:
Hu Gong, courtesy name Weichen, was registered in an officer household of the Left Imperial Guard in Nanjing. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather Hao was an Assistant Commander; his grandfather Kuan was an Assistant Regional Military Commissioner; his father was Ying, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed seventy-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Mu, courtesy name Weiqiao, was registered in a civilian household in Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Jingsheng held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his grandfather Zheng was Vice Commissioner of the Institute of Imperial Crafts and was granted the title of Secretary; his father Shen was a Prefect, and his mother, née Li, was granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ben and Zhu [?], and his younger brother was Cai. He married a woman née Li. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chao Bideng, courtesy name Ruji, was registered in a civilian household in the Pingyi Native Chief's Office, Mahu Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a native of Yibin County. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the nineteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yan; his grandfather Youwen was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father Chang was a Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Bifeng, and his younger brother was Bidi. He married a woman née Tian. He placed fifteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Zongli, courtesy name Bangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jingzhou, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi. An added-quota student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather Ning was posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather Yuan was a Prefect; his father Zheng was a District Magistrate; his mother was née Liu, and his stepmothers were née Liu and née Xue. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zongxing, Zongben, Zongxian, and Zongru. He married a woman née Han. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 232nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Feng Kui 馮夔, courtesy name Tingbo, was registered in the Confucian scholar household category in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather Shan and father Tai were both Instructors. His father's principal wife was Lady Qin, and his birth mother was Lady Li. Both parents were living. He married Lady Wang. He ranked thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zha Huan 查煥, courtesy name Wenxian, was registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twentieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuzhi, his grandfather Zonghan, his father Huan 桓, and his mother Lady Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tai and his younger brother Yu. He married Lady Xu. He ranked eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Huan 彭桓, courtesy name Jingwu, was registered in a civilian household in Jishui County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Butong 不同; his grandfather Rubi was an Instructor who received the honorary title of Compiler in the Hanlin Academy; and his father Dao was an Instructor. His mother was Lady Liu and his stepmother Lady Hu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji and Jie, the latter a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination year; his younger brothers were Fei, Mao, Cai, Ting, and Lai. He married Lady Zhang. He ranked seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Ji 朱稷, courtesy name Xiangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wengui, his grandfather Ziliang, and his father Yongjie. His father's former wife was Lady Chen, and his mother was Lady Zou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Zhi and Ji. He married Lady Liu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Hui 王惠, courtesy name Jifu, was registered in a civilian household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-seven years old, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shun; his grandfather, Lian; his father, Dongxi, held the honorary title of Charitable Official; and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jian, Dun, Zhen, Tai, and En, and his younger brother was Xian. His wife was née Weng. He placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 152nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Lai 鄭淶, courtesy name Zishui, was registered in a military household in Lin'an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, his family rank is recorded as “six-seven” [?]. He was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather, Xian, was a Registrar in a metropolitan county; his father was Shu; his mother was née Gao; and his stepmother was née Shao. He had living grandparents and parents. His younger brother was Pei, and his wife was née Tong. He placed seventy-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Ze 彭澤, courtesy name Jiwu, was registered in an official household of Lanzhou Guard, Shaanxi, and was originally from Changsha County, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first in his family and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Xuan; and his father, Ding. His father's former wife was née Zhao, and his mother was née Tang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Chong, and his wife was née Wu. He placed ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zongshang 李宗商, courtesy name Shangzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Leting County, Luanzhou Subprefecture, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second in his family and was thirty-four years old, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Botong; his grandfather, Sheng, was posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; and his father, Lin, was an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife was née Wang; his mother, née Tian, was granted the title of Lady (ruren); and his stepmother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zongxia, and his younger brothers were Zongzhou and Zongru. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hai Li 海鯉, registered in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yuezhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chaozong, Commissioner of a Salt Tax Office; his grandfather was Yongqing; and his father was Qi. His mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Xu. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His younger brothers were Jing, Tuo, Ao, Kun, Jiao, and Qiu. He married a woman née Xu. He placed forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shao Fen 邵蕡, registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wenshi; he ranked eleventh among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shufang, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Hongyu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his father was Hua. His mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Ying, Lan, Fan (a District Magistrate), Chai, Zhi, Kui, and Hui; his younger brothers were Zhuang, Zun, and Xun. He married a woman née Yan. He placed sixty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Hao 尹灝, registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the National University. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chunfu; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-nine years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhi; his grandfather was He, a Police Chief granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Ren, formerly a Surveillance Assistant Commissioner. His mother was née Li, granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brother was Hao 顥. He married a woman née Liu. He placed forty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Yong 黃顒, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bowang; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengzhen; his grandfather was Mo, a School Instructor; and his father was Gang. His father's former wife was née Lin, and his mother was née Fang. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Ang and Tang; his younger brothers were Juan, Wenyang, Wenzhang, Wenxiong, Wenrong, and Wenfeng. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed twenty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:

He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jieqing; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-seven years old, born on the second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Mengzhang, his grandfather Xianghui, and his father Chaoshen; his mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brother was Liangyong〔a jinshi of the same examination cohort〕, and his younger brothers were Liangsheng and Liangcai. His wife was née Huang. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Hong, registered in Xi’an County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dayou; he ranked first in birth order and was forty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shilian, his grandfather Daoqing, and his father Bin; his mother was née Zheng. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His younger brother was Hao. His wife was née Lü; he subsequently married a woman née Xia. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 136th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Gui, registered in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he ranked sixth in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Dade, his grandfather Yinglin, and his father Xian〔an honorary official〕; his mother was née Ming. Both his parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan, Shi〔an Investigating Censor〕, and Fu, and his younger brothers were Zhen and Zhi. His wife was née Lü. He placed twenty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Hu, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingrui; he ranked twenty-second in birth order and was forty-five years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Chang, his grandfather Du, and his father Guang; his mother was née Xu. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Shu, and his younger brother was Lin. His wife was née Zheng. He placed eighty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 141st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shen Heng, registered in an artisan household in Haiyan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Pingfu; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Boying, his grandfather Mengxian, and his father Wenyu; his mother was née Chen, and his stepmothers were née Hu and née Zhang. His father was living, and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Huang. He placed forty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mi, registered in a salt-producing household in Meizhou, Sichuan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingzuo; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twentieth day of the intercalary twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen; his grandfather Chaoyong was an Assistant Prefect; his father He was a student of the Imperial University; and his mother was née Ou. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Jian, and he married a woman née Cheng. He placed eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Pu, registered in a civilian household in Nanxi County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Kechun; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yong'an, his grandfather Chaozu, and his father Daoming; his mother was née Han. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xue, Zao, and Song, and he married a woman née Peng. He placed fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and two hundred seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Xun, registered in a civilian household in Chongqing Department, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the department school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruyong; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the eleventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Wende; his grandfather Zhongyuan received the honorary title of Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; and his father Qi was a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father's former wife, née Liu, received the title of Lady (ruren); his mother was née Ou. His mother was living, and his father deceased. His elder brother was Mi and his younger brother Yu; he married a woman née Deng. He placed fifty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Cong, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in an official household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, posthumously granted the title of Secretariat Drafter; his grandfather was Jin; and his father was Ao. His father's former wife was née Gao, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Huan, Xiu, Bi, and Zhen, and his younger brothers were Chen, Qi, Lian, Qi, and Lin. His wife was née Ni. He ranked sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 149th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guan Xian, courtesy name Rujun, was registered in a military household in Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingde; his grandfather was Youcai; and his father was Jue, posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Han, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother, née Zhao, was granted the same title. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Shou, an Honorary Official for Righteousness; Lian, a Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and Yi, a Medical Officer in a School of Medicine. His younger brother was Zhen. His wife was née Li. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 216th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zong You, courtesy name Yuanji, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fifteenth day of the intercalary eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxian; his grandfather was Shiying, granted the title of District Magistrate; and his father was Xian, a Registry Manager in the Censorate. His father's former wife, née Ren, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Service; his mother was née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xin, Wei, Jie, Zhuo, and Ji. His wife was née Zhang. He ranked seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Shan, courtesy name Tiyuan, was registered in a military household in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-four, and born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Weiqing; his grandfather was Tian; and his father was Zheng. His mother was née Wu, and his stepmother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Lai. He ranked third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sha Li, registered in Xuzhou in the directly administered region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daozhong; he ranked second in his family and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather Gui, and his father Jie, a Prefectural School Professor; his mother was née Zhou. His mother alone survived. His elder brother was Xingheng, and his younger brothers were Yongcheng and Yongji. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Huan. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Sheng, registered in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Keming; he ranked eighteenth in his family and was forty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Baowen, his grandfather Tianxiang, an Honorary Official, and his father Hongjing; his mother was née Qiu. His father alone survived. His younger brothers were Hao and Chun [?]. He married a woman née Fang. He placed thirty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Yunteng was registered in an illegible county and prefecture in Fujian; his household registration category is illegible. He was a county school student and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name, family ranking, age, and birth date cannot be recovered from the damaged text [?]. His great-grandfather was Yuanshan; his grandfather’s and father’s names and his mother’s surname are illegible. Both parents survived. His younger brother was Yunqiao. He married a woman née Guan. He placed seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jiong, registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Guangyu; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-two years old, born on the seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yijing, and his grandfather Shiwang held the conferred title of Vice Director of the Office of Transmission. His father Mu was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel; his mother, née Chen, held the conferred title of Lady (ruren). His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zhao, Xun, Lie, and Xuan. He married a woman née Lu. He placed fortieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:

His courtesy name was Shangzhi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the eighteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Weixiao, posthumously appointed Secretary; his grandfather was Li, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; and his father was Mo, an Imperial University student. His mother was née Mu and his stepmother née Ma; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gang, Hui, and Wang. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked forty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Rui 趙瑞, of Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was registered in a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Weide; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the tenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Junning, his grandfather Yongchuan, and his father Sen; his mother was née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qian, Rong, and Huan, and his younger brothers Rui [?] and Lin. He married a woman née Cai and subsequently a woman née Lin. He ranked seventieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 160th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yanqi 王彥奇, of Yunyang County, Kuizhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was registered in a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingjian; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fourth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Caijie, his grandfather Wenxiu, and his father Jingxian; his mother was née Xiang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yanyin and Yanzhang. He married a woman née Li. He ranked forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 139th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Pei 周珮, of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was registered in a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Mingyu; he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Shizhan, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Jilin, granted the title of Hanlin Compiler; and his father was Yu, a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His mother was née Zhu; his father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Fan. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Defu, his grandfather Bin, his father Yu, and his mother née Zhu; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Xuan (an honorary official for philanthropy), Huan, Min, and Jing (an Instructor in the Directorate of Education); his wife was née Pan; he placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Ji, registered in a military household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Anshi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-five, born on the seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiushi, his grandfather Pan (a District Magistrate), his father Zhen, his father's principal wife née Zhang, and his mother née Gao; both parents were deceased; his elder brother Jing was a student of the Directorate of Education; his wife was née Huo; he placed eighteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Wen, registered in a civilian household in Ninghai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhairen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the first day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deqing, his grandfather Wenlin, his father Zhongyu (an honorary official for philanthropy), and his mother née Ye; both parents were living; his younger brothers were Ji, Geng, Cheng, Leng, and Yi; his wife was née Wang; he placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Xiangming, registered in a civilian household in Huangyan County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chongzhe, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yancheng, his grandfather Zhidao, his father Shike, his father's former wife née Zhou, and his mother also née Zhou; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Xiangqi; his wife was née Lin, and his subsequent wife was also née Lin; he placed forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zai, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zikun. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-three and was born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheqi, his grandfather Fuxian, and his father Ning. His father's principal wife was née Xie; his stepmothers were née Liu, Lei, and Zheng; his birth mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jian, and his younger brothers were Yi, Yan, and Jie. He married a woman née Jin. He placed twenty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Chen, registered in Yingshan County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yaozuo. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-eight and was born on the first day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi, his grandfather Li, his father Yingkui, and his mother née Ren. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xiang. He married a woman née Kang. He placed thirteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Huang, registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Tingshi. Twelfth in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and was born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shunmao; his grandfather Min was a District Magistrate; and his father Chang was a former Instructor. His mother was née Deng, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Huan; his younger brothers were Zhang and Lian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jian, registered in Lanyang County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Kongzhao. First in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the seventeenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen; his grandfather Rong was a Vice Commissioner of a Salt Distribution Commission; and his father Qi was a District Vice Magistrate. His mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Qin, Yue, and Quan. He married a woman née Wen. He placed thirteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Yuanzuo; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, an Instructor; his grandfather was Xin; his father was Dayou, Monitor in the Directorate of Education; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Pu, and his wife was née Wu. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Yi, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Xizhi; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the eleventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonglian; his grandfather was Shicheng; his father was Yu; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xing, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Xu; his younger brothers were Chen, Mian, Zao, Xuan, Dun, and Yun. His wife was née Pan. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 236th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Rou, registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenzheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chang; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Sen; and his mother was née Ge. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Gang, and his younger brother was Shen. His wife was née Zhu; he subsequently married a woman née Xu. He placed fifty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lü Jie belonged to a military household registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Tingchen; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-seven years old, born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fazhen; his grandfather was Qing; his father was Hong, an Usher in the Court of State Ceremonial; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Fang and Fu, and his wife was née Chen. He placed eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 172nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

His courtesy name was Xuanfu; he was third in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the first day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Gongjun, his grandfather Minzhong, and his father Zhi, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Zuo. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Fuxiang and Tingxiang, and his younger brother Kaoxiang. His wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Chen, registered in an officer household of the Shenwu Right Guard and originally from Jia County, Henan, was a student of the prefectural school of Zhiding [?], specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Juzhan; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Neng, posthumously granted the title of Company Commander, and his father Lin, a Company Commander. His mother, née Li, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace; his stepmothers were née Ren, invested with the title of Lady of Peace, and née Shi. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Huan, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ting, registered in a Confucian scholar household in Wan’an County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xianzhuo; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the seventeenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Junying, posthumously granted the title of Minister of Justice; his grandfather was Guanghua, his father Shuxun, and his mother née Peng. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Chi and Tuan, and his wife was née Xiao. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Shiwei, registered in a civilian household in Xuanping County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shimei; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Junpu, his grandfather Zicong, and his father Ze, a Registrar. His legal mothers were née Zheng and née Dai, and his birth mother was née Ren. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Shizuo, Shiyou, and Shifang, and his wife was née Liang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Lu 李祿, registered in a military household in Tangyin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongxue, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the sixth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qin, his grandfather Sheng, his father Jie, and his mother née Shi; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zhen and Zuo, and his younger brother was You; he married a woman née Zhao. He placed thirty-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liao Ji 廖紀, registered in a civilian household in Dongguang County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingchen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhaoxing, his grandfather Youneng, and his father Xuan; his father's former wife was née Chen, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chun; he married a woman née Guo and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji 劉績, registered in a military household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yongxi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-three, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Ying, his father Xingfu, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Yu; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Lun and Shou, the latter a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brothers were Xi and Ji; he was betrothed to a woman née Xi. He placed eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third Class: 205 men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) by equivalence.

Zhu Xiang, registered in Cangzhou, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingrui; he ranked first among his brothers, was forty-four years old, and was born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather Cheng was a Chief Clerk; his grandfather Zan was an Instructor; his father Mao was a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chengfang, registered in Jiayu County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Maoqing; he ranked fifth among his brothers, was forty-one years old, and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather Ying was a Police Chief, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief; his grandfather Shan was an Instructor, likewise posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Censor-in-chief; his father was Shen, and his mother was née Deng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Chengye and Chengheng; his younger brothers were Chengji, a tribute scholar, Chengxun, and Chengshi. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Lu, registered in Chuzhou in the directly administered region, belonged to a military household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunsheng; he ranked second among his brothers, was twenty-seven years old, and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yu; his grandfather Quan was granted the title of Right Vice Minister; his father Cheng was Right Vice Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial; and his mother, née Wang, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Zhu, and his younger brother was Lin. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 214th in the Metropolitan Examination.
