translation_en:
Wang Jing, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenji; he ranked fifth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhiyi; his grandfather, Kewang; his father, Li, a county magistrate; and his mother, née Xu. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Wei, Cai, Hong, and Le, and his younger brother was Wei. His wife was née Lu. He placed eighty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Hong was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Shangyu County, Zhejiang. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Derong; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged forty-two, born on the fourth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Keshun, formerly a secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Mengpu; his father, Qi; and his mother, née Luo. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ting, Xiang, and Tang, and his younger brothers were He and Xiao. His wife was née Hu. He placed seventeenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 286th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Kui, registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Guowen; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongchao; his grandfather, Sihui, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; his father, Qianpu; and his mother, née Huang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bi, Lou, Jing, and Zhen. His wife was née Peng. He placed ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin, registered in Liquan County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zaizhong; he ranked second in his family and was aged thirty-two, born on the twentieth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youdao; his grandfather, Lun; his father, Tong; his mother, née Dong; and his stepmother, née Gao. His father and stepmother were living. His elder brother was Xuan, and his younger brothers were Jian, Yong, Rui, and Gang. His wife was née Wei. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
方憲〔貫福建興化府莆田縣竈籍，國子生，治詩經，字宜弼，行五，年三十六，十二月二十四日生〕。曾祖積善，祖夢周，父休徵〔贈員外郎〕，母王氏〔贈宜人〕，繼母黃氏。慈侍下，兄宗伋〔楚府教授〕、誌、守〔參政〕、彬〔刑部主事〕，弟宏。娶柯氏，繼娶李氏。福建鄉試第二名，會試第一百六十一名。

陸坦〔貫直隸蘇州府吳縣匠籍，國子生，治詩經，字子由，行四，年三十七，四月十四日生〕。曾祖誠，祖凱，父澂，母沈氏。具慶下，兄巽〔訓導〕、垕、濟，弟垣、埅、坤。娶沈氏。應天府鄉試第一百三十五名，會試第二十名。

曹玉〔貫山東兖州府嘉祥縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷珮，行三，年四十，十一月初六日生〕。曾祖彥貞，祖敏，父通，母周氏。永感下，兄福、貴，弟珖、琛、璽、諫。娶李氏。山東鄉試第七十五名，會試第二百四名。

羅列〔貫廣東廣州府南海縣民籍，府學生，治詩經，字天爵，行一，年三十，九月十一日生〕。曾祖祖昌，祖勝宗，父廣成，母招氏。具慶下，弟剛、釗。娶潘氏。廣東鄉試第二十六名，會試第一百十九名。
translation_en:
Fang Xian, courtesy name Yibi, was registered in a salt-producing household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fifth in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jishan; his grandfather, Mengzhou; and his father, Xiuzheng, posthumously appointed Vice Director. His mother, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother surviving. His elder brothers were Zongji [?] (Professor in the household of the Prince of Chu), Zhi, Shou (Administration Vice Commissioner), and Bin (Secretary in the Ministry of Justice); his younger brother was Hong. He married a woman née Ke and subsequently a woman née Li. He placed second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Tan, courtesy name Ziyou, was registered in an artisan household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Kai; his father, Cheng; and his mother, née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xun (Assistant Instructor), Hou, and Ji; his younger brothers were Yuan, Fang, and Kun. He married a woman née Shen. He placed 135th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Yu, courtesy name Tingpei, was registered in a civilian household in Jiaxiang County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third in birth order and was forty years old, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhen; his grandfather, Min; his father, Tong; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu and Gui; his younger brothers were Guang, Chen, Xi, and Jian. He married a woman née Li. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Lie, courtesy name Tianjue, was registered in a civilian household in Nanhai County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in birth order and was thirty years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuchang; his grandfather, Shengzong; his father, Guangcheng; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Gang and Zhao. He married a woman née Pan. He placed twenty-sixth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

崔侃〔貫山西太原府陽曲縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字廷直，行六，年二十五，十月初一日生〕。曾祖敏，祖忠〔贈戶部郎中〕，父能〔郎中〕，前母卜氏〔贈宜人〕，母高氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄儀、儼、俊〔省祭官〕、傑、伸，弟仁，娶王氏。山西鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百八十五名。

陳珩〔貫廣西桂林府全州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字君錫，行五，年三十五，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖得善，祖啟，父潮〔知縣〕，母梅氏。慈侍下，兄珙、璲、璉，弟瑀〔陰陽學正術〕、珝、瑞、珍，娶蔣氏。廣西鄉試第十八名，會試第一百十三名。

来天球〔貫浙江紹興府蕭山縣，竈籍，國子生，治書經，字伯韶，行七，年三十三，八月二十八日生〕。曾祖名，祖宗表，父雄，嫡母王氏，生母孔氏。慈侍下，兄珪、瑭〔貢士〕、瓚〔義官〕、瑚、璉、璠、璵，弟璘，娶戴氏。浙江鄉試第七十四名，會試第二百九名。

金山〔貫河南開封府歸德州夏邑縣，民籍，縣學生，治易經，字仲仁，行二，年二十七，四月初六日生〕。曾祖熙，祖禮〔封刑部員外郎〕，父醞〔參政〕，母朱氏〔封宜人〕。重慶下，兄巽〔義官〕，弟磐、江，娶李氏。河南鄉試第二名，會試第五十六名。
translation_en:
Cui Kan, registered in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingzhi, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather, Zhong, was posthumously appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Neng, was a Director; his father’s former wife, née Bu, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his mother, née Gao, held that title. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Yi, Yan, Jun (a Sacrificial Attendant), Jie, and Shen, his younger brother was Ren, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Heng, registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junxi, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was thirty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Deshan, his grandfather was Qi, his father was Chao, a County Magistrate, and his mother was née Mei. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Gong, Sui, and Lian, and his younger brothers were Yu (Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang), Xu, Rui, and Zhen; his wife was née Jiang. He placed eighteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lai Tianqiu, registered in Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Boshao, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was thirty-three, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather was Zongbiao, and his father was Xiong; his legal mother was née Wang, and his birth mother was née Kong. His mother was living and his father deceased; his elder brothers were Gui, Tang (a tribute scholar), Zan (an honorary official), Hu, Lian, Fan, and Yu, his younger brother was Lin, and his wife was née Dai. He placed seventy-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Shan, registered in Xiayi County, Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county government school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongren, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-seven, born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Xi; his grandfather, Li, was granted the title Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Yun, was an Administration Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Zhu, held the title Lady of Suitability. His parents and grandparents were living; his elder brother was Xun (an honorary official), his younger brothers were Pan and Jiang, and his wife was née Li. He placed second in the Henan Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

尹禄〔貫陝西秦州衛籍，盩厔縣人，國子生，治詩經，字廷璽，行三，年四十，五月二十三日生〕。曾祖成，祖政，父文慶，母宋氏。永感下，兄玉、璽，弟獻，娶趙氏。陝西鄉試第十六名，會試第二百七十一名。

洪鐘〔貫江西撫州府崇仁縣軍籍，翰林院秀才，治詩經，字聲和，行七，年二十八，二月初四日生〕。曾祖子庸，祖孟莊，父朝宗〔兵馬司吏目〕，母吳氏。具慶下，兄本彝、卣彝、鼎，娶吳氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百九十五名。

朱華〔貫四川重慶府長壽縣民籍，麻城縣學訓導，治禮記，字素卿，行二，年三十五，十月二十一日生〕。曾祖廷恕，祖得先，父璉，母劉氏。具慶下，兄萬，娶劉氏。四川鄉試第三十二名，會試第六十八名。
translation_en:
Xu Ao, registered with the Chengdu Rear Guard in Sichuan and originally from Putian County, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Pengju; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yijin, his grandfather Fuzu, his father Xian, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His wife was née Zheng. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Lu, registered with the Qinzhou Guard in Shaanxi and originally from Zhouzhi County, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingxi; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Zheng, his father Wenqing, and his mother née Song. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yu and Xi, and his younger brother was Xian. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hong Zhong, of military household registration in Chongren County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a Cultivated Talent (xiucai) of the Hanlin Academy, specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Shenghe; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Ziyong, his grandfather Mengzhuang, his father Chaozong, a Clerk in a Wardens' Office, and his mother née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Benyi, Youyi, and Ding [?; the division of the names is uncertain]. His wife was née Wu. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Hua, of civilian household registration in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Assistant Instructor at the Macheng County School, specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Suqing; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tingshu, his grandfather Dexian, his father Lian, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Wan, and his wife was née Liu. He placed thirty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 弘治三年進士登科錄
text:

鍾永〔貫順天府大興縣民匠籍，直隸吳縣人，府學生，治詩經，字世昌，行一，年三十一，三月三十日生〕。曾祖徐保，祖文，父振，母張氏。慈侍下，弟瑀、舉。娶富氏。順天府鄉試第二十二名，會試第二百八十三名。

李琳〔貫山西太原府平定州民籍，州學生，治書經，字廷貢，行三，年二十八，七月二十三日生〕。曾祖思〔訓導〕，祖恭，父倫，母趙氏，繼母張氏。具慶下，兄璇、瓛。娶袁氏。山西鄉試第八名，會試第一百七十九名。

汪淵〔貫直隸徽州府歙縣民籍，國子生，治春秋，字仲深，行一，年三十二，三月十一日生〕。曾祖子益，祖用本，父中〔貢士〕，母徐氏。具慶下，弟漢、濟、清、淋、澄、澂。娶鄭氏。應天府鄉試第一百十四名，會試第七十二名。
translation_en:
Wang Tong, registered in a scholarly household in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Biyuan; he ranked twentieth in birth order and was forty years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Sijing; his grandfather was Ruwei, a Prefectural School Professor; his father was Dalun; and his mother was née Feng. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Xian, a Department Magistrate; Chang, a District Magistrate; Sheng, an Assistant Prefect; Heng; and Tai. His younger brothers were Rui, Jin, Xiang, Jian, and Jie. He married a woman née Rao and subsequently a woman née Ni. He placed third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhong Yong, registered in a civilian-artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and originally from Wu County in Zhili, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shichang; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-one years old, born on the thirtieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xubao; his grandfather was Wen; his father was Zhen; and his mother was née Zhang. His mother alone was still living. His younger brothers were Yu and Ju. He married a woman née Fu. He placed twenty-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 283rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Lin, registered in a civilian household in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tinggong; he ranked third in birth order and was twenty-eight years old, born on the twenty-third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Si, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Gong; his father was Lun; his mother was née Zhao; and his stepmother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan and Huan. He married a woman née Yuan. He placed eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuan, registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Zhongshen; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the eleventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Ziyi; his grandfather was Yongben; his father was Zhong, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han, Ji, Qing, Lin, Cheng (澄), and Cheng (澂). He married a woman née Zheng. He placed 114th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

沈冬魁〔貫直隸河間府阜城縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字伯貞，行一，年二十七，十月初一日生〕。曾祖爾卿，祖景先，父泉，母陸氏。慈侍下，弟夏元，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第二十名，會試第二百五十一名。

馬繼祖〔貫直隸揚州府泰州如皋縣，民籍，縣學生，治禮記，字崇功，行一，年四十一，十二月初七日生〕。曾祖通，祖定〔贈衛經歷〕，父俊〔衛經歷〕，嫡母范氏〔封孺人〕，生母傅氏。慈侍下，弟繼宗，娶田氏。應天府鄉試第三十名，會試第一百六名。

包溥〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字民敬，行十四，年三十五，二月初三日生〕。曾祖文助，祖甸，父鑑，前母何氏，母胡氏。慈侍下，兄澄、澤〔貢士〕、濟、浩，弟瀚、渙、滋、沂〔監生〕、治、潭，娶汪氏。浙江鄉試第三十一名，會試第一百四十八名。

吳潛〔貫江西撫州府臨川縣，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字顯之，行一，年三十三，十二月初一日生〕。曾祖世彰〔義官〕，祖天常〔封文林郎主事〕，父南立〔義官〕，母張氏。重慶下，弟涓、浩、瀹、源、濬、洙、泗，娶李氏。江西鄉試第十名，會試第九十七名。
translation_en:
Shen Dongkui, registered in Fucheng County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Bozhen; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-seven, born on the first day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Erqing, his grandfather Jingxian, his father Quan, and his mother née Lu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Xiayuan, and his wife was née Li. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 251st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Jizu, registered in Rugao County, Taizhou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Chonggong; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-one, born on the seventh day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tong; his grandfather Ding was posthumously appointed Registrar of a Guard, and his father Jun served as Registrar of a Guard. His father's principal wife was née Fan, granted the title Lady (ruren), and his birth mother was née Fu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Jizong, and his wife was née Tian. He placed thirtieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bao Pu, registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Minjing; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and was thirty-five, born on the third day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhu, his grandfather Dian, and his father Jian; his father's former wife was née He, and his mother was née Hu. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Cheng, Ze (a tribute scholar), Ji, and Hao; his younger brothers were Han, Huan, Zi, Yi (a student of the Directorate of Education), Zhi, and Tan. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Qian, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xianzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-three, born on the first day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Shizhang was an honorary official; his grandfather Tianchang was granted the titles Gentleman of Cultivated Learning and Secretary; his father Nanli was an honorary official, and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Juan, Hao, Yue, Yuan, Jun, Zhu, and Si, and his wife was née Li. He placed tenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Jiang 胡江 was registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Donghui, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziyu; his grandfather, Xianxiang; and his father, Shiduan. His mother was née Deng, and his stepmothers were née Chen and née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His wife was née Tu. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiao Shu 喬恕 was registered in Ningling County, Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Xiren, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was He; his grandfather, Liang; his father, Min; and his mother, née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Que, Xian, Yu, and De. His wife was née Chen. He placed seventieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and seventy-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Wen 楊文 was registered in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Zongzhou, ranked third among his brothers, and was forty-five years old, born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Demin; his grandfather, Jicheng; his father, Gongshi; and his mother, née Hua. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ren and Shao. His wife was née Cai. He placed second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Sheng 譚昇 was registered with the Yingzhou Central屯 Guard [?] and was a native of Gan County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shijin, ranked first among his brothers, and was thirty-nine years old, born on the ninth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinghui; his grandfather, Zihe; his father, Lun; and his mother, née Sun. Both his parents were living. His younger brother was Gao. His wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Jian 俞諫, courtesy name Liangzuo, was registered in a civilian household in Tonglu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county government student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked twenty-fifth in family birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongbin; his grandfather, Zongzheng; his father, Jin, a department magistrate; and his mother, née Zhang. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brother was Bing, and his younger brother Hui held the honorary title of “charitable official” (yiguan). He married a woman née Chai and subsequently a woman née Shao. He placed twenty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nie Xian 聶賢, courtesy name Chengzhi, was registered in an artisan household in Changshou County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family birth order and was thirty years old, born on the fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Zixin; his father, Lian, a department judge; and his mother, née Xu. His father alone was surviving. His younger brother was Chun. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed sixty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventy-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Gui 郭桂, courtesy name Shifang, was registered in a military household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the thirtieth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a county magistrate under the Yuan dynasty; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Huan; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were surviving. His younger brothers were Huai, Liang, and Mei. He married a woman née Yu. He placed sixteenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Feng 宋鳳, courtesy name Yingshao, was registered in a civilian household in Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked fourth in family birth order and was thirty-seven years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wende; his grandfather, Zheng, assistant director of the Office of Animal Breeding; his father, An; and his mother, née Dong. His mother alone was surviving. His elder brothers were Qi, an Imperial University student, Lin, and Shuang; his younger brothers were Peng, Ying, and Wu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 120th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lai Xian, registered in Yongding County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boqi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-one, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zulong, an Imperial University student; his grandfather was Zongxin, and his father was Heng. His father's former wives were née Huang and née Liu; his mother was née Li, and his stepmother was née Lan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zuanxian and Rongguang, and his wife was née Que. He placed thirteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Yue, registered in Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Weizhi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bencheng, his grandfather was Jing, his father was Huai, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rui, Ming, Yu, and Quan; his younger brothers were Xuan, Zhen, and Qin. His wife was née Yu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 260th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cong Lan, registered in Wendeng County, Ninghai Subprefecture, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military artisan household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingxiu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Junzhong, his grandfather was Shirong, his father was Chun, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi and Kui, and his wife was née Xing. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Song, registered in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a scholar household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Qingcheng; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the twenty-seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chuandao; his grandfather was Ying, an Instructor; and his father was Lun, who received the salary of a Chief Administrator. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xu; his younger brothers were Jun, Dun, Ting, and Ti. His wife was née Wang. He placed third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Song 陸淞, registered in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wendong. Seventh in birth order, he was twenty-five years old, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zongxiu, honored as a Righteous Commoner; his grandfather was Gui, an honorary official for longevity; and his father was Chang, a National University student. His mother was née Cao. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Pu, a National University student, Yuan, Ji, Chun, Hong, and Wei; his younger brothers were Yi, Huai, Hao, and Han. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Ming 鄧明, registered in Zi County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Weiyuan. Second in birth order, he was thirty-two years old, born on the third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Rang, his grandfather was Benshan, and his father was Lin, a county school Instructor. His father's principal wife was née Bao, and his birth mother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Chang, and his younger brother was Jing. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked eighteenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and one hundred twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Fu 黃傅, registered in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Mengbi. Sixth in birth order, he was thirty years old, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Chuo; his grandfather was Shuang, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; and his father was Zhi. His mother was née Tang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Zuo, You, Fu, Wei, and Jia; his younger brothers were Yu and Ru. He married a woman née Cheng. He ranked forty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Che Liang 車梁, registered in Shi Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a National University student. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Maoxian. First in birth order, he was thirty-six years old, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, a Master of Divination (dianshu); his grandfather was Kezhao, who had been honorifically appointed Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his father was Lei, also a Master of Divination. His mother was née Wu. His father was deceased, and he attended his living mother. His younger brothers were Huan and Tang, both National University students; Xiang, a Medical Director; Yue; and Gai. He married a woman née Zhang and subsequently married another woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Jing, courtesy name Dalun, was registered in a military household in Ningxiang County, Changsha Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Jifu; his grandfather, Zuda; his father, Shengliang; and his mother, née Huang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Ning and Ben, and his wife was née Li. He ranked forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Yue, courtesy name Qizhi, was registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fifteenth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bozhuang; his grandfather, Wenxin, posthumously granted the title of Supervising Secretary; his father, Lin, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Wang, granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased, and he attended upon his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ying, Tang, Kai, and Hua; his younger brothers were Wu, Luan, Lian, Rui, Zong, Ao, Tian, Lin, and Zhong. His wife was née Sun. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Guan, courtesy name Tingwang, was registered in a civilian household in Fengxiang County, Fengxiang Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather, Lun; his father, Xi, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Gun, and his wife was née Li. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Xuan, courtesy name Dehe, was registered in a military artisan household of the Imperial Bodyguard and was a native of Jiaxing County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Xian; his grandfather, Zhongyu; his father, You; his mother, née Sheng; and his stepmother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Rong and Cheng, and his wife was née Wang. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Kai, registered in a civilian household in Li County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenxiang; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Hong, his grandfather Zhong, and his father Ju, a National University student; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Yuan, and his younger brothers were Jie, Ding, and Ning. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Rui, registered in a military household in Yongnian County, Guangping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Dunzhi; he was third in birth order, aged forty-two, and born on the eighth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhongliang, his grandfather Youliang, and his father Ning, an official awaiting selection for appointment. His father's former wife was née Bai, his mother née Cheng, and his stepmother née Zhang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yue and Qi. He married a woman née Li and subsequently another woman née Li. He placed seventy-second in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Wuqing, registered in a civilian household in Haining County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongxun; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zihua, posthumously appointed Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Right; his grandfather Ziliang and father Zhang were both Administration Vice Commissioners of the Right. His mother, née Fang, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His elder brother was Wenqing; his younger brothers were Zhongqing, an Instructor in the Yin-Yang School, and Zhengqing. He married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Wang. He placed fifty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Min, registered in a medical household in Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Weiqin; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twentieth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Guan, an Instructor in the Medical School; his grandfather was Wei, his father Jin, and his mother née Huang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Xiang and Wen, and his younger brothers were Qi, Zhao, Dun, and Zheng. He married a woman née Feng. He placed 126th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Sui 劉璲, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Shiyue; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Congxian, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Xun, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; his father was Zhongzhou, Magistrate; and his mother was née Dong. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yu, and his wife was née Qin. He placed sixty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jingming 張景明, registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingguang; he ranked fourteenth among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Bi; his grandfather was Yunhui, granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War; his father was Yixian; and his mother was née Yuan. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jingkui, and his younger brothers were Jingsui and Jingcan. His wife was née Shen. He placed seventieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 181st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Qin 趙欽, registered in Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Sijing; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ling; his grandfather was Decheng; his father was Yu; and his mother was née Wang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Jian, and his younger brothers were Yue and Jin. His wife was née Wu. He placed nineteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Tingyi 李廷儀, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites. His courtesy name was Mingfeng; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Tianyi; his grandfather was Bing; his father was Sheng, granted the title of Secretary; and his mother was née Deng, granted the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tingshao, Instructor, and Tingmei, Prefect; his younger brother was Tingfang, an honorary official. His wife was née Huang. He placed fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yuan Zonggao, registered in an official household in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zhongde; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the fourteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouxian; his grandfather was Siming, granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Kai, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong; and his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady for Service. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Zongkui, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Zongji, Zongqi, Zongyin, Zongwang, and Zonglong. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yao, registered in a military household in Anding County, Gongchang Prefecture, Shaanxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xiangqian; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lin, an Administrative Assistant; his grandfather was Wu, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father was Sheng, a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; and his mother was née Zhang, granted the title of Lady of Peace. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Luan and Wu, both National University students, and Yan. He married a woman née Yang. He placed thirty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jing, registered in a civilian household in Changning County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tenghai; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the sixteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui; his grandfather was Zhongzhen, posthumously granted the title of Hanlin Academy Compiler; his father was Yongzong; and his mother was née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ao; his younger brothers were Lin and Kun, both tribute scholars (gongshi), Ying, Yong, a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites, Liang, Fang, and Shi. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed fifty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Yinghe, registered in a civilian household in Dazhu County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chunyuan; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinde; his grandfather was Bin; his father was Sizhi; and his mother was née Deng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yingjie, and his younger brothers were Yingduan and Yingshi. He married a woman née Tao. He placed sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 158th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Xie, registered in Changshan County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yongzhong. He ranked fourteenth among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty-four, born on the first day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shantong, an Honorary Official for Righteousness; his grandfather was Gai; his father was Shi; and his mother was née Mao. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Yu, and his younger brothers were Yi and Xing. He married a woman née Jiang and subsequently a woman née Yan. He placed sixty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Qin, registered in Gu’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuegong. He ranked first among his brothers and male cousins and was aged forty, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youxin; his grandfather was Gui; his father was Duan; and his mother was née Yang. His mother alone survived. He married a woman née Lü and subsequently a woman née Zu. He placed 109th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Jizong, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zijing (秄敬 [?]). He ranked second among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-three, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wuhe; his grandfather was Mujiu; and his father was Yue. His parents and grandparents were deceased. He married a woman née Du. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Lun, registered in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dajing. He ranked third among his brothers and male cousins and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao; his grandfather was You, a County Vice Magistrate; his father was Cong; his mother was née Li; and his stepmother was née Su. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Duo and Ming, and his younger brother was Wei. He married a woman née Hou. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

徐鉞〔貫湖廣武昌府興國州軍籍，國子生，治書經，字用寧，行二，年三十八，九月二十九日生〕。曾祖宗一，祖友貴，父政〔贈御史〕，母從氏〔封太孺人〕。慈侍下，兄鏞〔知府〕，弟欽、鉱〔憲王全同科進士〕、鏜、鎧、鎰、鍊，娶馮氏。湖廣鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百五名。

鄭士忠〔貫廣東廣州府東莞縣竈籍，國子生，治易經，字廷獻，行二，年三十一，八月十八日生〕。曾祖克初，祖耿彰，父誠，母麥氏。具慶下，兄士敬，娶方氏。廣東鄉試第十四名，會試第一百九十一名。
translation_en:
Xu Jue, courtesy name Xinzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Wu County in Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Pu, his grandfather Zongyuan, his father Pu 溥, and his mother née Tao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Zhen, Jiuchou, and Jiugong; his wife was née Fan. He ranked 128th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 280th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shizhong, courtesy name Daofu, was registered in a military household in Huang County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Lian, a District Magistrate, his father Zuan, a Guard Registrar, and his mother née Qin. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brothers were Lun and Jia; his younger brothers were Shiyong, Ru, Shizheng, and Jie. His wife was née Yan. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yue, courtesy name Yongning, was registered in a military household in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zongyi, his grandfather Yougui, and his father Zheng, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor. His mother, née Cong, was granted the honorific title Tai Ruren, an official’s mother’s title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yong, a Prefect; his younger brothers were Qin, Kuang [the annotation here is garbled: “Prince Xian, all metropolitan graduates of the same cohort” [?]], Tang, Kai, Yi, and Lian. His wife was née Feng. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Shizhong, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a salt-producing household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Kechu, his grandfather Gengzhang, his father Cheng, and his mother née Mai. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shijing, and his wife was née Fang. He ranked fourteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Jin, registered in a civilian household in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chaozhen, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was forty years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongwen, his grandfather Tingchang, and his father Lin, who had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under the applicable regulations; his mother was née Wang, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zheng, Xuan, and Qiong, Assistant Magistrate of Xiajin County; his younger brothers were Xian, Zhang, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Qing, and An. He married a woman née Wu. He placed fourteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 130th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Botong, registered in a military household in Tongshan County, Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Benrui, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-four years old, born on the first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kexuan, his grandfather Fuxing, and his father Chaozhang; his mother was née Zhou, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Boxian, Boqi, Bozhi, Boming, and Bokui. He married a woman née Xie. He placed eleventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 203rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Guan, registered in a civilian household in Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yanguan, he ranked sixth among his brothers, and he was forty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhirang, his grandfather Pixun, and his father Xunyue; his mother was née Luo and his stepmother née Ao. His father alone was living. His younger brother was Yanmeng, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Wenkui, registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Xizeng, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was forty-one years old, born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bojin, his grandfather Jianyuan, and his father Liangren; his mother was née Dai, and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Wenbo and Wenlin. He married a woman née Tong. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zou Yu 鄒虞, registered with the Hangzhou Front Guard in Zhejiang and a native of Xingan County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianxiang; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bifu, his grandfather Mengkui, and his father Gui, who had been granted the cap and girdle of official status under an applicable regulation; his mother was née Yao. His father alone was still living. His wife was née Lu. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jing 王璟, of civilian registration in Jianshui Subprefecture, Lin'an Prefecture, Yunnan, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Mingzhong; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the intercalary sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shanji, his grandfather Zheng, his father Ying, and his mother née Hong. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Xuan. His wife was née Zhu; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Cheng 彭誠, of civilian registration in Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Junshi; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuanda, his grandfather Chengyuan, and his father Kun, a saltworks superintendent; his mother was née Liu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Weixin, a student of the Directorate of Education, Weichong, and Weishou. His wife was née Xu. He placed seventy-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mo Ying 莫英, of civilian registration in Dao Subprefecture, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Zhongyi; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-three years old, born on the twelfth day of the intercalary fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhilong, his grandfather Sheng, a tribute scholar, and his father Jun; his mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Yang. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Fang, and his wife was née He. He placed fortieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 233rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sun Yong 孫鄘, courtesy name Aozhi, was registered in a civilian household in Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the seventh day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kai, his grandfather Jie, and his father Ji; his mother was née Ma and his stepmother née Mei. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Yin, and he married a woman née Chen. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Lian 蔡鍊, courtesy name Maocheng, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the fourth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boyan, his grandfather Shumeng, and his father Bin; his mother was née Qi. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin, a Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, and Jian; his younger brothers were Lu, Jin, and Lian. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Jing 丘經, courtesy name Zhengfu, was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Anji County, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Wei, and his father Ying; his mother was née Gu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Lun, and he married a woman née Li. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Xuan 董宣, courtesy name Chaoyong, was registered in a civilian household in Cao Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty-six, and born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Yuanshan, and his father Ying, an honorary official for charitable contributions. His legal mother was née Liu, and his birth mother née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Kuang Jing, courtesy name Ruming, was registered in a civilian household in Gao’an County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the seventeenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanlin; his grandfather, Dalu; his father, Wanmou; and his mother, née Zou. Both parents were living. His wife was née Wu. He placed fifty-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Bingzhong, courtesy name Tianxu, was registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Lin, a Police Chief; his father, Duo, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Bingyi, and his wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Fengyi, courtesy name Tianrui, was registered in a military household in Xiangyuan County, Luzhou Subprefecture, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Record of Rites, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng; his grandfather, Duan, a Director of a County School posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father, Jie, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother, née Li, who had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). His father was deceased and his mother living. His younger brother was Fengming, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 154th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Feng, courtesy name Yingjue, was registered in a civilian household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Decheng; his grandfather, Tingji; his father, Shuji; and his mother, née Gu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Peng and He, and his wife was née Gu. He placed fiftieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ru Luan 茹鑾, courtesy name Shihe, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Hong was a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Shi; his father Yu was a County Magistrate; and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Mou 鍪, Jian 鑒, Zhen 鎮, and Jian 鑑, and his wife was née Gu. He placed ninety-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu You 徐有, courtesy name Ruowu, was registered in an artisan household in Luoshan County, Xinyang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Caisi; his grandfather was Tong; his father Wenchang was a Prefectural School Professor; and his mother was née Shi. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Shi, and his wife was née Yin. He placed twenty-second in the Henan Provincial Examination and 116th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Xi 孫璽, courtesy name Guoxin, was registered in a civilian household in Qingcheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shixian; his grandfather was Jingwen; his father was Qin; and his mother was née Ding. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Chong and Hui, his younger brothers were Shan and Bi, and his wife was née Jia. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Jing 曹敬, courtesy name Deyu, was registered in a civilian household in Gaocheng County, Zhending Prefecture, Zhili. A National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the sixth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhong; his grandfather was Bin; his father was Zhigang; and his mother was née Yao. His father alone was living. His elder brothers were Neng and Yu, the latter an official awaiting selection for appointment, and his wife was née Fan. He placed eighty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 111th in the Metropolitan Examination.

王鉞〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字懋揚，行七，年四十二，二月十四日生〕。曾祖祚，祖召南，父克厚，母趙氏。永感下，兄館〔訓導〕、鎗、錕、鈇、鑼，娶徐氏，繼娶孟氏。浙江鄉試第八名，會試第一百六十七名。

戴乾〔貫浙江台州府臨海縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字元之，行二，年二十七，四月二十八日生〕。曾祖孟淵，祖廷祥，父仲仁，母金氏。慈侍下，兄聰，弟巽，娶侯氏。浙江鄉試第五十七名，會試第九十一名。
translation_en:
Zhang Gang, registered with the Suzhou Guard in Zhili and a native of Xingan County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tingjie, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was forty-one years old, born on the fourth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Yuan, his father Cong, and his mother Lady Chen; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Qin, Zhao, and Kai; he married Lady Su and subsequently Lady Hua, and placed 125th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Kai, of civilian registration in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongfan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was forty-three years old, born on the eleventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zuping, his grandfather Kai 愷, his father Jing, and his mother Lady Zhou; both parents were deceased; his younger brothers were Lin, Mo, Qi, Gui, Tang, and Di; he married Lady Zhang and placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yue, of civilian registration in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Maoyang, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was forty-two years old, born on the fourteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Zuo, his grandfather Zhaonan, his father Kehou, and his mother Lady Zhao; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Guan (an Assistant Instructor), Qiang, Kun, Fu, and Luo; he married Lady Xu and subsequently Lady Meng, and placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Qian, of civilian registration in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Mengyuan, his grandfather Tingxiang, his father Zhongren, and his mother Lady Jin; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Cong and his younger brother Xun; he married Lady Hou and placed fifty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and ninety-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

趙維藩〔貫直隸真定府元氏縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字价夫，行一，年二十九，七月二十六日生〕。曾祖鑑，祖福貴〔巡檢〕，父彛〔監生〕，母魏氏，繼母劉氏。慈侍下，弟維垣、維屏、維寧、維有，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十六名，會試第十八名。

陶煦〔貫浙江嘉興府秀水縣，軍籍，縣學生，治詩經，字時和，行四，年二十五，九月初六日生〕。曾祖鉦〔義民〕，祖濟民，父松，母張氏。重慶下，兄勳、熈、燁，弟照〔同科進士〕、燦、儒、儼、俸、烈、煒、煉，娶唐氏。浙江鄉試第七十七名，會試第一百三十一名。

彭惟方〔貫江西吉安府安福縣，民籍，國子生，治春秋，字重義，行六，年三十八，十一月二十一日生〕。曾祖原脩，祖翔高〔義官〕，父箴省，母周氏。慈侍下，兄惟中、惟正，弟惟直，娶賀氏。江西鄉試第六十八名，會試第一百三十八名。
translation_en:
Wang Xian, registered in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Weigang. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-four, and born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jingzu, his grandfather Hai, and his father Zhi; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhi 志, Min 忞, and Si 思. His wife was née Liu. He ranked eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Weifan, registered in Yuanshi County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jiefu. He was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Jian; his grandfather Fugui was a Police Chief, and his father Yi was an Imperial University student. His mother was née Wei and his stepmother née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Weiyuan, Weiping, Weining, and Weiyou. His wife was née Wang. He ranked 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Xu, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shihe. He was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Zheng held the honorary designation “Righteous Commoner”; his grandfather was Jimin and his father Song. His mother was née Zhang. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Xun, Xi, and Ye; his younger brothers were Zhao (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), Can, Ru, Yan, Feng, Lie, Wei, and Lian. His wife was née Tang. He ranked seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Weifang, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zhongyi. He was sixth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Yuanxiu; his grandfather Xianggao held honorary official status, and his father was Zhensheng. His mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Weizhong and Weizheng, and his younger brother was Weizhi. His wife was née He. He ranked sixty-eighth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 138th in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳玭〔貫福建漳州府龍溪縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字子懷，行一，年三十六，十一月初五日生〕。曾祖敏雍，祖仲〔知縣〕，父玉文，母蔡氏。永感下，弟頊、珝，娶郭氏。福建鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百五十六名。

translation_en:
Zhao Shiyuan 趙士元 was registered in a military household of Hezhou Guard, Shaanxi, and was a student of the guard school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Junpin; he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Jing, his father Ying, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His wife was née Zhang. He placed tenth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Ze 周澤 was registered in a civilian household in Jiashan County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. He was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tianyu; he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenhua, his grandfather Huan, his father Jie, and his mother née Zhou. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Huai, and his wife was née Qiu. He placed first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Pin 吳玭 was registered in a military household in Longxi County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zihuai; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minyong, his grandfather Zhong (Magistrate), his father Yuwen, and his mother née Cai. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Xu 頊 and Xu 珝, and his wife was née Guo. He placed forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tang Kui 唐夔 was registered in a civilian household in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongshao; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zh廷 Zhiting, his grandfather Ming (County Vice Magistrate), his father Xi, his mother née Wang, and his stepmother née Jiang. His father and stepmother were living. His younger brothers were Ru 儒, Fu 傅, Long 龍, Zuo 佐, Chu 俶, Yi 伊, Qiao 僑, Yi 億, and Zhuan 僎; his wife was née Zhao. He placed eleventh in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

路麟〔貫江西吉安府安福縣，儒籍，國子生，治春秋，字肇治，行二，年三十七，十一月二十二日生〕。曾祖世清〔贈左參政〕，祖斐澳〔遇例冠帶〕，父元，母周氏。具慶下，兄重，弟煥、尚、燁、孝、承、隆、建、銘、邵、鶴。娶周氏，繼娶孫氏。江西鄉試第四名，會試第一百十二名。

黎民牧〔貫湖廣岳州府華容縣，軍籍，國子生，治書經，字本恕，行五，年三十六，正月十二日生〕。曾祖仕禎〔贈吏部右侍郎〕，祖斌〔縣丞，贈吏部右侍郎〕，父淳〔南京禮部尚書〕，母金氏〔封淑人〕。嚴侍下，兄民獻〔貢士〕，弟民表〔進士〕、民衷、民安、民俊、民信。娶張氏。湖廣鄉試第八十一名，會試第一百三十五名。

周冕〔貫直隸池州府貴池縣，民籍，府學生，治詩經，字尚文，行二，年三十二，三月二十二日生〕。曾祖璿，祖鑑，父崑〔訓導〕，母吳氏。具慶下，兄宿，弟宇、宙。娶呂氏。應天府鄉試第八十九名，會試第八十九名。

郭濬〔貫直隸真定府平山縣，軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字舜德，行一，年四十，九月初七日生〕。曾祖祖，祖清，父敦〔縣丞〕，母賈氏。慈侍下，弟濠。娶吳氏，繼娶彭氏。順天府鄉試第六十五名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
Lu Lin, registered in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a scholar household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zhaozhi, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shiqing, posthumously granted the title of Left Administration Vice Commissioner; his grandfather was Feiao [?], granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his father was Yuan, and his mother was née Zhou, both living; his elder brother was Zhong, and his younger brothers were Huan, Shang, Ye, Xiao, Cheng, Long, Jian, Ming, Shao, and He; he married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Sun, and placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Minmu, registered in Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Benshu, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six, born on the twelfth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shizhen, posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Personnel; his grandfather was Bin, a County Vice Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Minister of Personnel; his father was Chun, Minister of Rites at Nanjing, and his mother was née Jin, granted the title Lady of Gentleness; his father alone was still living; his elder brother was Minxian, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and his younger brothers were Minbiao, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Minzhong, Min’an, Minjun, and Minxin; he married a woman née Zhang and placed eighty-first in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Mian, registered in Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shangwen, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather was Jian, his father was Kun, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother was née Wu, both parents living; his elder brother was Su, and his younger brothers were Yu and Zhou; he married a woman née Lü and placed eighty-ninth in both the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jun, registered in Pingshan County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili), belonged to a military household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shunde, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was forty, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zu [?], his grandfather was Qing, his father was Dun, a County Vice Magistrate, and his mother was née Jia; his mother alone was still living; his younger brother was Hao; he married a woman née Wu and subsequently a woman née Peng, and placed sixty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

常元慶〔貫陝西西安府乾州，民籍，國子生，治詩經，字宗善，行一，年三十六，五月二十三日生〕。曾祖允中，祖伯通，父翥〔教諭〕，母閻氏，繼母朱氏。慈侍下，弟元良、元吉、元佐，娶鄧氏。陝西鄉試第七名，會試第五十二名。
translation_en:
Xiao Juyuan, courtesy name Yongpu, was registered in Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the thirtieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, his grandfather Sicai, and his father Zhenlun (an Honorary Official); his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ji, Han, and Chun, and he married a woman née Li. He placed forty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Qin, courtesy name Jingzhi, was registered in Huangmei County, Qizhou Subprefecture, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Fatong, his grandfather Boyuan, and his father Yong (a National University student); his mother was née Fu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yue, Yue, Kai, and Jian (鉞、鑰、鎧、鑑), and he married a woman née Wu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Chong, courtesy name Lianbi, was registered in Guangzhou Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Ning, his grandfather Min, and his father Zhidao (Commander of a Military Police Office); his mother was née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qi, and he married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and two hundred forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Yuanqing, courtesy name Zongshan, was registered in Qianzhou Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the National University specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-third day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong, his grandfather Botong, and his father Zhu (an Instructor); his mother was née Yan and his stepmother née Zhu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His younger brothers were Yuanliang, Yuanji, and Yuanzuo, and he married a woman née Deng. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and fifty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.
