董紱，貫湖廣黃州府麻城縣，軍籍，國子生。治《春秋》，字嗣紳，行七，年三十二，正月十七日生。曾祖南壽，祖潮〔檢校〕，父應軫〔按察司僉事〕，嫡母徐氏，繼母王氏，生母魏氏。慈侍下，兄緒〔貢士〕、紹、綬、縡、繣、繪〔舉人〕、紘〔進士〕，弟統。娶陳氏，繼娶周氏。湖廣鄉試第四名，會試第九十名。

蕭淵，貫山東東昌府堂邑縣，軍籍，國子生。治《春秋》，字文靜，行二，年三十六，三月初九日生。曾祖敬，祖貞〔知州〕，父瑛〔通判〕，母劉氏。永感下，兄漢〔義官〕。娶趙氏。山東鄉試第十五名，會試第一百九十四名。

王哲，貫直隸蘇州府吳江縣，軍籍，縣學生。治《易經》，字思德，行二，年三十四，五月二十五日生。曾祖湜，祖恭，父宗吉，前母于氏，母沈氏。具慶下，兄賢〔義官〕，弟明〔監生〕、敏。娶申氏。應天府鄉試第二十四名，會試第九十八名。

羅賢，貫山西太原府清源縣，民籍，國子生。治《詩經》，字大用，行一，年三十七，十二月初七日生。曾祖景思，祖滿，父公海，母徐氏，繼母曹氏。具慶下，弟良、方、智。娶陳氏。山西鄉試第四十二名，會試第八十四名。
translation_en:
Dong Fu, registered in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Sishen. Seventh in birth order, he was aged thirty-two and was born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Nanshou; his grandfather was Chao, an Examiner (jianjiao); and his father was Yingzhen, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His legal mother was née Xu, his stepmother née Wang, and his birth mother née Wei. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Xu, a tribute scholar (gongshi), Shao, Shou, Zai, Hua, Hui, a provincial graduate (juren), and Hong, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi); his younger brother was Tong. He married a woman née Chen and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninetieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Yuan, registered in Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Wenjing. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the ninth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jing; his grandfather was Zhen, a Department Magistrate; his father was Ying, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Han, an honorary official (yiguan). He married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Zhe, registered in Wujiang County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Side. Second in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shi; his grandfather was Gong; and his father was Zongji. His father's former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Shen. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xian, an honorary official (yiguan); his younger brothers were Ming, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Min. He married a woman née Shen. He placed twenty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Xian, registered in Qingyuan County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dayong. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the seventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jingsi; his grandfather was Man; his father was Gonghai; his mother was née Xu; and his stepmother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Liang, Fang, and Zhi. He married a woman née Chen. He placed forty-second in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Wei, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Minwang. He ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Kongli; his grandfather, Yanchi, held the conferred title of Bureau Secretary; his father, Mian, was a Prefect; and his mother, née Liang, held the conferred title of Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Ying and Wei [?]. He married a woman née Gan. He placed thirty-fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Dajing, registered in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to an artisan household and was a county government school student. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zhengzhi. He ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the eighth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Liang; his grandfather, Jingyu; his father, Shiying; and his mother, née Shi. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Daji, Daxu, Dachun, Daji, Dashen, and Dashou. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed eighty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Wei, registered in Lizhou, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a subprefectural government school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Shiyuan. He ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-eight years old, born on the fifth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongli; his grandfather, Ji; his father, Qi; and his mother, née Yu. Both his parents were living. His elder brother was Shen, and his younger brothers were Ren and Yi. He married a woman née Li. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Tingchun, registered in Duchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Yuanzhi. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bojie; his grandfather, Zixuan, was a Station Master; his father was Jiuzhou; and his mother was née Zhou. Both his parents were deceased. His elder brother was Tingjie. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Wenfu, registered in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an additional student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yidao; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-four years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Jingchang, his grandfather Jun, his father Ci, and his mother née Zhu. His grandparents and parents were living. His elder brother was Wenying and his younger brother Wenzuo. He was betrothed to a woman née Liang. He placed second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 117th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chang Ji, registered in Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Huifu; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the sixth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Quan, his grandfather Jing, his father Zan (a subprefectural Clerk), and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Qing (an Instructor), and his younger brothers were Yuan, Zhun, and Shen. His wife was née Wang. He placed sixteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zan, registered in Guo County, Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongqi; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Xuan, his father Yue (a Granary Commissioner), and his mother née Nie. Both parents were living. His wife was née Xiao. He placed thirty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 137th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Mo, registered in Licheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rujia; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhongxin, his grandfather Lianggui, his father Zi, and his mother née Yang. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Fang, Long (an honorary official for charitable contributions), and Yan. His wife was née Wang. He placed twentieth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 231st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Han, courtesy name Kerong, was registered in Boping County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mingyou; his grandfather, Zhigang; his father, Bin, a Chief Clerk; and his mother, née Sun. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Chao, and his wife was née Li. He ranked sixty-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 201st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Jue, courtesy name Tianjue, was registered in Gushi County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenbin; his grandfather, Ziming; his father, Wan; and his mother, née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brother was Chen, and his wife was née Duan. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xi Shu, courtesy name Wentong, was registered in Suining County, Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. An added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was first in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sigong; his grandfather, Xuan; his father, Zuxian; and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shi, Ji, Chun, and Tuan, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lu, courtesy name Tianxi, was registered in Huaiji County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the third day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fozuo; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Jixue, a Commissioner (office unspecified); and his mother, née Guo. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Feng and Yi, and his wife was née Liang. He ranked eighteenth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉棠〔貫山東濟南府章丘縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字思召，行二，年四十，十一月十三日生〕。曾祖仲英，祖誠〔知縣〕，父灝，母黃氏，繼母趙氏。嚴侍下，兄榆，弟棟，娶賈氏。山東鄉試第五十五名，會試第一百二名。

胡雍〔貫寬河衞官籍，山西臨縣人，國子生，治春秋，字伯雍，行一，年三十三，七月初九日生〕。曾祖斌〔百戶〕，祖全〔指揮僉事〕，父安〔指揮僉事〕，母趙氏〔封恭人〕。嚴侍下，娶呂氏，繼娶申氏。順天府鄉試第四十名，會試第二百八十七名。

郭綸〔貫陝西西安府華州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字大綸，行三，年四二，十月初二日生〕。曾祖謙，祖整，父信，母曹氏，繼母潘氏。慈侍下，兄仁、淳，弟紀〔監生〕、純，娶董氏。陝西鄉試第四十一名，會試第一百七十名。
translation_en:
Liu Wenchong, courtesy name Yuanxi, was registered in a military household of the Wuxiang Left Guard and was a native of Yutian County, Jizhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuchuan, his grandfather Hai, his father Chun, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Peng. He placed sixty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tang, courtesy name Sizhao, was registered in a civilian household in Zhangqiu County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhongying; his grandfather Cheng was a District Magistrate; his father was Hao, his mother née Huang, and his stepmother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brother was Yu and his younger brother Dong. His wife was née Jia. He placed fifty-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Yong, courtesy name Boyong, was registered in an officer household of Kuanhe Guard and was a native of Lin County, Shanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather Bin was a Company Commander; his grandfather Quan and father An were both Assistant Commanders. His mother, née Zhao, was granted the title Lady of Respect. His father was living and his mother deceased. His wife was née Lü; he subsequently married a woman née Shen. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 287th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Lun, courtesy name Dalun, was registered in a civilian household in Huazhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A subprefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-two [?; transcribed as 四二], born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian, his grandfather Zheng, his father Xin, his mother née Cao, and his stepmother née Pan. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Ren and Chun (淳); his younger brothers were Ji, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Chun (純). His wife was née Dong. He placed forty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lu Yi, registered in an artisan household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Fengchong; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fourth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Hong; his father, Cong, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Gu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Fu and Han, and his younger brother was Zhu. He married a woman née Wei. He placed thirty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 146th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Chongxi, registered in a civilian household in Shizhou, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenming; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shizhen; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Dai, a District Magistrate; and his mother, née Li. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was Chonghui, an honorary official for public benefactions; his younger brothers were Chongdao, a sacrificial attendant [?], Chongqing, and Chongming, an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Huo. He placed twelfth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ye Yongxiu, registered in a civilian household in Dongguan County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Rushi; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the eleventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zuquan; his grandfather, Jingfang; his father, Qing, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Zhu. His mother alone was still living. He married a woman née Li. He placed eighteenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Dading, registered in an officer household of the Fujun Guard and a native of Xinyang Subprefecture, Henan, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongxian; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather, Dao, and grandfather, Lin, were each posthumously awarded the title of Vice Commander; his father, Xian, was a Vice Commander. His mother, née Mei, was invested with the title of Grand Lady of Purity. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ding, a Vice Commander, and Nai, a Squad Leader entitled to wear the official cap and belt. He married a woman née Ding and subsequently a woman née Fan. He placed forty-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Du Kai, courtesy name Gongshi, was registered with Fuyu Guard and was a native of Jishui County, Jiangxi; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuande; his grandfather, Dapeng; and his father, Bang, an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his mother, née Wei, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother Huan was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites, and his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-fifth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Xuan, courtesy name Tianqi, was registered in a military household in Fenzhou, Shanxi; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged forty-one, and was born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi; his grandfather, Yu; and his father, Fu, a District Magistrate; his father's former wife was née Liu, and his mother was née Ren. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi and Yuan, his younger brother was Ji, and his wife was née Han. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Yishou, courtesy name Tianhe, was registered in a military household in Baling County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-nine, and was born on the twenty-fourth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yiwen; his grandfather, Li, a District Vice Magistrate; and his father, Gongfu, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Shao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lushou, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Qishou; his younger brothers were Qiaoshou and Songshou. His wife was née Liu, and he subsequently married a woman née He. He placed seventy-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Rushi, courtesy name Ruoxu, was registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Huazhou, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi; an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked third among his brothers, was aged twenty-seven, and was born on the second day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Kai; and his father, Wu; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan and Kun; his younger brothers were Rong, Xian, Ding, Huan, and Wan; and his wife was née Yuan. He placed fifty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

治詩經字文中行四年三十二十二月二十六日生
曾祖崇本　祖孟頴〔訓導贈主事〕父泗〔兵部員外郎〕　母袁氏〔封安人〕

茅光著〔貫浙江寧波府慈谿縣，軍籍，儒士，治《詩經》，字日升，行四，年四十三，五月初九日生〕。曾祖天麒，祖惟揚〔按察使〕，父蓁〔理問〕，母桂氏。永感下，兄光霽，弟光大。娶桂氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第二百六十三名。

余敬〔貫廣東廣州府新會縣，民籍，國子生，治《書經》，字行簡，行四，年三十六，三月十八日生〕。曾祖妙成，祖琳〔遇例冠帶〕，父肄〔教諭〕，母謝氏。具慶下，兄讓〔訓導〕、紹夔〔通判〕、士龍，弟章、正義。娶周氏。廣東鄉試第四名，會試第六十二名。

饒塘〔貫江西南昌府進賢縣，民籍，府學生，治《詩經》，字文中，行四，年三十一，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖崇本，祖孟頴〔訓導，贈主事〕，父泗〔兵部員外郎〕，母袁氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄述，弟燧。娶夏氏。江西鄉試第四十名，會試第二百五十五名。
translation_en:
Lü Tang, registered in Jinzhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Tingshao; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Jie, was a Granary Commissioner, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; and his father, Zheng, was Left Administration Vice Commissioner. His father's former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother was also née Liu. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Qi, a Medical Instructor; Xuan, an Imperial University student; and Kai. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Liu. He ranked 111th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Mao Guangzhu, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a Confucian scholar. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Risheng; he was fourth in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tianqi; his grandfather, Weiyang, was a Surveillance Commissioner; his father, Zhen, was a Case Reviewer; and his mother was née Gui. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Guangji, and his younger brother was Guangda. He married a woman née Gui. He ranked twelfth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Jing, registered in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Xingjian; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Miaocheng; his grandfather, Lin, had been granted the privilege of wearing official cap and girdle under applicable regulations; his father, Yi, was a County School Instructor; and his mother was née Xie. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Rang, an Assistant Instructor; Shaokui, an Assistant Prefect; and Shilong. His younger brothers were Zhang and Zhengyi. He married a woman née Zhou. He ranked fourth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Tang, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Wenzhong; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Chongben; his grandfather, Mengying, was an Assistant Instructor, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father, Si, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of War; and his mother, née Yuan, had been granted the title of Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shu, and his younger brother was Sui. He married a woman née Xia. He ranked fortieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 255th in the Metropolitan Examination.

杜宏〔貫河南開封府許州臨潁縣，民籍，縣學生，治書經，字淵之，行二，年三十六，十二月二十二日生〕。曾祖興，祖賢，父瑄，母宋氏。具慶下，兄林，弟宗章，娶介氏。河南鄉試第十八名，會試第二百九十六名。

translation_en:
Meng Hui, courtesy name Yunji, was registered in Cangwu County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the sixteenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shouyuan, his grandfather Bao, his father Quan, and his mother née Du. His mother alone was still living. His elder brother was En, and his wife was née Ouyang. He ranked twelfth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Xi, courtesy name Zongyu, was registered with Zhenwu Guard in Shanxi and was a native of Shouzhou in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged forty, and born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Gui, his father Duo (a Prefectural Judge), and his mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingbi, Tinglian, Tingke, and Tingpei, and his wife was née Feng. He ranked forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Hong, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was registered in Linying County, Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Xian, his father Xuan, and his mother née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Lin, his younger brother Zongzhang, and his wife was née Jie. He ranked eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jie, courtesy name Chaoyong, was registered in Pingding Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Jing (Chief Clerk of the Right Chief Military Commission), his father Shan (an Instructor in the Yin-yang School), and his mother née Yan. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Kan (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and his wife was née Zhu. He ranked forty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Fan Zhang 范璋, registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Bangxian, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-one, born on the twentieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingzhao, his grandfather Hao, and his father Duan, an honorary official recognized for public benefaction; his mother was née Wu, both parents were living, his elder brothers were Tinghui, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Tingcai, likewise an honorary official recognized for public benefaction, his wife was née Wu, and he placed thirty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Zhen 吳珎, registered in a salt-producing household in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Meizhong, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged forty-two, born on the fifth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qingzhi, his grandfather Dingyuan, and his father Rang; his mother was née Tang, both parents were living, his elder brothers were Zhang and Wan and his younger brother Jie, his wife was née Zhao, and he placed fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Zheng 陸徵, registered in a military household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shixiu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji, his grandfather Shizhen, and his father Ang; his father's principal wife was née Hao and his birth mother née Tao, the entry records both parents as living, his younger brothers were Yu, Hui, Che, and Wei, his wife was née Lü, and he placed eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zang Feng 臧鳳, registered in a civilian household in Qufu County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruizhou, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanshi, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Ji, an Assistant Instructor posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his mother, née Li, was granted the title of Grand Lady of Peace and was living, while his father was deceased, his elder brothers were Qi and Lin, the latter a Secretary in the Ministry of Works, his younger brother was Luan, he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Kong, and he placed first in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 221st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Biao, courtesy name Renjie, was a student of the National University from Baocheng County, Hanzhong Prefecture, Shaanxi, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Documents, was fifth in birth order, and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Puqing; his grandfather, Fulong; his father, Hong; and his mother, née Wan. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Longhai, Longzhun, Longzhen, and Longyuan. He married a woman née Deng. He ranked twenty-ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 220th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Xiyan, courtesy name Zongzhe, was a student of the National University from Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, registered in a military household. He specialized in the Book of Odes, was first in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Er; his grandfather, Shun; his father, Bin; and his mother, née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Xizeng, Xisi, Ximeng, Ximin, and Xiran. He married a woman née Wang. He ranked forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 262nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Deng Wenzhi, courtesy name Ruzhong, was an added-quota student of the prefectural school from Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a civilian household. He specialized in the Book of Documents, was third in birth order, and was aged twenty-nine, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Yu; his father, Ju; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenjie and Wenyuan; his younger brothers were Wenshan, Wenxiu, Wenxian, and Wenming. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked thirty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 168th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin, courtesy name Ruqi, was a student of the National University from Chaoyi County, Tong Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, registered in a military household. He specialized in the Book of Changes, was third in birth order, and was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zuo; his grandfather, Ju, was Commissioner of a Tax Office; his father, Bin, was an Unranked Clerk; and his mother was née Kong. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Jie and Yuan. He married a woman née Shang [?]. He ranked twenty-first in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 278th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Cunli, registered in a civilian household in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was an additional student at the prefectural school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jingwen; his grandfather, Pu, held the honorary designation of Righteous Official; his father, Ming, was a Prefectural Assistant Magistrate; and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Cunren, and his wife was née Jiang. He placed seventy-third in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Ran, registered in a civilian household in Jing County, Ningguo Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yunzhi; he was first in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather, Chuzhong, was an Instructor of Medicine; his grandfather, You’ang, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his father was Mengxian; and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Lu, Fu, and Xin, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed twentieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 290th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Xi, registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jinghe; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tai; his grandfather, Zhen; his father, Zhong; and his mother, née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhan and Xi (睎). His first wife was née Zhang, and his subsequent wife was also née Zhang. He placed 104th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lin Tinghuan, registered in a military household in Wuchuan County, Huazhou Subprefecture, Gaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Gongqi; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the thirteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chong; his grandfather, Rong; his father, Huan; and his mother, née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother, Tingyu, was a student of the Directorate of Education; his younger brother was Tingyou; and his wife was née Li. He placed sixtieth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wan Xuan, registered in a military household in Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Tingqi; he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Fubi, a Messenger; his grandfather was Jian; his father was Shu, a County School Instructor; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xun, Lin, and Xi, the last a Magistrate; his younger brothers were Ying, Long, Hu, and Qi. His wife was née Sun. He placed forty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Xiqi, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the National University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Menglun; he ranked thirteenth in birth order and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Shujing; his grandfather was Mian, a Magistrate posthumously granted the title of Censor; and his father was Tixiang, granted the title of Vice Director. His father’s former wife, née Liu, was posthumously granted the title of Lady of Suitability; his mother, also née Liu, was granted the same title. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xiyuan, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangxi; Xidan; Xiyu; Ximin, an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; Xiran; and Xixian. His wife was née Liu. He placed eighteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zi, registered in a military household in Dingxing County, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianze; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zeng; his grandfather was Qian; and his father was Bin, a Registry Manager in a Pacification Commission. His mother was née Shen, and his stepmother was née Kong. His father was living, and his mother was deceased. His younger brothers were Xun and Run. His wife was née Mi. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Gang, registered in a civilian household in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the National University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Keli; he ranked fifth in birth order and was thirty-five years old, born on the thirteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Feng; his grandfather was Yu; and his father was Zhen, a Records Examiner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother was née Wang, and his stepmother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing, a National University student; Lun; Jin, an honorary official; and Shen, an honorary official. His younger brother was Ji. His wife was née Xu. He placed twentieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Sheng, registered in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Sifu, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged forty-eight, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonggeng, his grandfather Yizhong, and his father Shimi; his mother, née Jiang, was a chaste widow. His mother alone survived, and he attended upon her; his elder brothers were Zhen’an, Ke’an, and Yun’an, and his wife was née Yang. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Cong, registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Minde, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jing, his grandfather Ze, and his father Xun; his mother was née Ji. Both parents were living; his younger brothers were Ming and Zhi, and his wife was née Chen. He placed seventy-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Lian, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Zongqi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuying, his grandfather Chen, a District Magistrate, and his father Xi; his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Zhang, his younger brothers were Cheng, Zan, Jue, Huan, Zhen, and Wang, and his wife was née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 234th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qin Rui, registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Kejin, he ranked eighth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the sixth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hao, his grandfather Gui, and his father Cheng; his mother was née Shen. His mother alone survived, and he attended upon her; his elder brothers were Jian, a student of the Imperial University, and E; his younger brothers were Luan, Bin, 𨥥 (reading uncertain [?]), and Chong, and his wife was née Zhao. He placed thirty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Xi, registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Shixun, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-nine years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Shu, was an Assistant Instructor; his father was Lang, and his mother was née Qian. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Qian. He placed twenty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jing Zuo, registered in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Liangbi, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-six years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Minyuan; his grandfather was Ju; his father, Zhang, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; and his mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jie, Kan, and Xin, and his wife was née Lei. He placed eleventh in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Zhang, registered in Xiaogan County, De'an Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural government school student specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingyi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was twenty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yusheng; his grandfather, Zhao, held the honorary title of Official for Righteousness; his father, Min, was an Administrative Judge; and his mother was née Zhou. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tian and Gui, his younger brother was Zan, and his wife was née Li. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and two hundred eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Zhi, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Record of Rites; his courtesy name was Jingshan, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty years old, born on the thirteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xingtai; his grandfather, Zhixuan, had been granted the title of Secretary; his father was Can, and his mother was née Liu. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Tu, Bing, and Ya, and his wife was née Jin. He placed tenth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Ying, his father Jun, and his mother Lady Jiao; both parents were living; his younger brother was Jue, and his wife was Lady Xu; he placed eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 199th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Fenglai 彭鳯来, courtesy name Taihe, was registered in a military household in Huangpi County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang; he was a county government student specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked third in his family, and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhao, his grandfather Wanyi, his father Chang, an Assistant Prefect, and his mother Lady Yan; his mother alone was living; his elder brothers were Fengyi, an official awaiting selection for appointment, and Fengli, and his wife was Lady Zhou; he placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Guan 鄭瓘, courtesy name Wenqing, was registered in a civilian household in Lanxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang; he was an Assistant Instructor at the Min County government school, specializing in the Book of Changes, ranked seventeenth in his family, and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuncheng, his grandfather Di, an Administrator, his father Qi, a District Magistrate, and his mother Lady Wang; both parents were living; his elder brother was Fan, his younger brothers were Xu and Beng, and his wife was Lady Xu; he placed fortieth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Qing 許慶, courtesy name Yingzhen, was registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, ranked first in his family, and was aged forty-three, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Gongyi, his grandfather Wenli, his father Shun, his mother Lady Huang, and his stepmothers Ladies Qin and Yu; his mother alone was living; his younger brothers were Kai, Chen, Xin, and Bian, and his wife was Lady Yin; he placed 107th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Zan, registered in Penglai County, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zongyong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bozhong, his grandfather Sirong, his father Zhen, and his mother née Liu; both parents were living. His younger brothers were Cheng and Huan, and his wife was née Qu. He placed twelfth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jin'en, registered in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tianxi; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yijing, his grandfather Yongshou, his father Yuqing, and his mother née Weng; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yuan, Jinfang, Chuan, Ding, Qi, Shun, and Zhao, and his wife was née Lu. He placed thirteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Ju, registered in Teng County, Wuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chaohui; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged forty, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongxian, his grandfather Hui, his father Si, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were deceased. His first wife was née Chen, and his subsequent wife was née Li. He placed second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zuo Zhang, registered in Linchuan County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tinggui; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunming, his grandfather Bixi, his father Xinhou, and his mother née Hu; his parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Zan, Zhen, and Yao, and his wife was née Peng. He placed thirteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李師儒〔貫直隸保定府安州高陽縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字宗正，行九，年三十二，十一月初四日生〕。曾祖進，祖甫榮〔贈主事〕，父儼〔南京戶部郎中〕，母郭氏〔封安人〕。具慶下，兄俊、聰、敏、師孔、睿，娶于氏。順天府鄉試第十九名，會試第八十八名。
translation_en:
Xu Yu 徐鈺, registered in Xingguo Subprefecture, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yongli, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was twenty-five, born on the twenty-seventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongyi, his grandfather Yougui, and his father Xiao; his mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Huang, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yong, a Prefect; Yue, a metropolitan graduate of the same examination year; and Qin, an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Kai, Tang, Jian, and Lian. His wife was née Li. He placed thirteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jie 李傑, registered in Hancheng County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to an artisan household and was a Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Renying, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was forty-two, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanzhen, his grandfather Mian, and his father Rang; his mother was née Liu and his stepmother née Gao, and both parents were living. His elder brother was Jun and his younger brother Ren. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Mianren 公勉仁, registered in Mengyin County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shangde, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was twenty-nine, born on the third day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, a County Vice Magistrate; his grandfather was Ping; his father was Shu, a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zengren and Xingren, and his younger brothers Jingren, Liren, and Juren. His wife was née Kan. He placed seventy-fifth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiru 李師儒, registered in Gaoyang County, Anzhou Subprefecture, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a Directorate of Education student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zongzheng, he ranked ninth among his brothers, and he was thirty-two, born on the fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin; his grandfather was Furong, posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father was Yan, a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his mother was née Guo, invested with the title of Lady of Peace. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jun, Cong, Min, Shikong, and Rui. His wife was née Yu. He placed nineteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ding, registered in a civilian household in Julu County, Shunde Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhongqi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the fifteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Deming; his grandfather was Wengui, a Registrar; his father was Wei; and his mother was née Li. His parents and grandparents were deceased. His elder brother was Yong, an Assistant Instructor, and his younger brothers were Zi and Zhen; his wife was née Qiao. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 125th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Hui, registered in a civilian household in Shidai County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yunzhi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-four, born on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Deshao; his grandfather was Sheng; his father was Wang, an Imperial University student; and his mother was née Shao. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Can, and his wife was née Shu. He placed fifty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 114th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xia Sheng, registered with the Hainan Guard in Guangdong and originally from Dingyuan County in the Metropolitan Region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Jingxi, he ranked second in birth order, and he was aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Junyi; his grandfather was Li; his father was Xuan; his legal mother was née Zhong; and his birth mother was née Sun. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Shi, Min (an Assistant Instructor), Zhang, and Wei; his wife was née Lu. He placed forty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 267th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Qia, registered in a civilian household in Fuyang County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yunren, he ranked eighteenth in birth order, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Yixian; his grandfather was Shizhang; his father was Hong; and his mother was née Tang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ji, Yi (沂), Zhu, and Pang; his younger brothers were Hao (浩), Yi (湙), Hao (濠), Ying, Shang (漡), and You; his wife was née Sun. He placed twenty-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Fu, registered in Yibin County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Rude; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Zhiyuan, and his father Gang; his mother was née Tao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bi, Qing, and Xiang, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Youji, registered in Yueqing County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Suzheng; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty years old, born on the fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guan, a District Magistrate; his grandfather was Pu, and his father Mian; his mother was née Chen. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother was Youzhi, and his wife was née Huang. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 294th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Duo, registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was an added-quota student at the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chaolu; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was forty years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yiliu, his grandfather Dasi, and his father Tijing; his mother was née Zhu and his stepmother née Lin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Lin, Ying, Lang (an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), Gan, and Xu; his younger brother was Rui, and his wife was née Dai. He placed eighty-first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jin, registered in Guangde Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianxiang, his grandfather Sizheng, and his father He; his mother was née Shen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yong, Ang, Yu, and Fu; his younger brothers were Zhou and Han, and his wife was née Cao. He placed seventy-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Pu, registered in Huaining County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili, in a military household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Gongji, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged forty, born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Rulin; his grandfather, Yong, was a medical officer; his father, Yu, was an assistant prefect; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Qing, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yu, registered in Wendeng County, Ninghai Subprefecture, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in an artisan household, was an added-quota student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Meizhi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the fourteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Shineng, his grandfather Xianming, his father Qing, and his mother née Wang. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brother was Xuan, and his wife was née Wang. He placed thirteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and eightieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Xuan, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, in a civilian household, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingxian, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the twenty-fifth day of the intercalary ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wu, his grandfather Li, his father Qin, and his mother née Dang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Rong, his younger brothers were Cong and Zan, and his wife was née Liu. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Shu, registered in an official household of the Taiyuan Left Guard in Shanxi and originally from Gaoyou Subprefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; his courtesy name was Tianze, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Zhigao; his grandfather, Jing, was a company commander; his father, Bi, was an investigating censor; and his mother, née Yan, had been granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Han, was a tribute scholar (gongshi); his younger brothers were Jing, a company commander, Hong, and Kuang. His wife was née Jiang, and his subsequent wife was née Zhu. He placed sixty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Fu, courtesy name Chunfu, was registered in a military household in Ningyuan County, Daozhou, Yongzhou Prefecture, Huguang; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanwen, his grandfather Junchang, and his father Yuanzhi, an honorary official of the eighth rank; his father's former wife was née Feng and his mother née He; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Chang and his younger brothers Gun, Ke, Shi, Ai, Xun, Shu, Yu, and Xuan; he married a woman née Liu and subsequently a woman née Xiang; he ranked sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qiu Jun, courtesy name Bangyan, was registered in an artisan household in Xinhe County, Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the fifth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Xin, his father Song, and his mother née An; his parents and grandparents were living; his elder brother was Ren and his younger brothers Jie, Zuo, and You; he married a woman née Li; he ranked ninety-eighth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 115th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Guang, courtesy name Shihong, was registered in a civilian household in Wuxi County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengqian, his grandfather An, a County Vice Magistrate, his father Minbiao, and his mother née Zhao; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Xu and his younger brother Lian; he married a woman née Zhou and subsequently a woman née Hou; he ranked 103rd in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 193rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhai Jing, courtesy name Xingjian, was registered in a civilian household in Yishi County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; he was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents, second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congshan, his grandfather Yong, his father Tong, and his mother née Xie; both parents were deceased; his elder brother was Xuan; he married a woman née Jing and subsequently a woman née Chen; he ranked thirty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Fang, courtesy name Dexin, was from Wuqing County, Tongzhou Subprefecture, Shuntian Prefecture, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Dequan, his grandfather Rong, and his father Zhong; his mother was née Zhang and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His wife was née Hao. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Hong 徐浤, courtesy name Benshen, was from Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, and belonged to a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked eighty-seventh in his generation and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhong, his grandfather Siwen, and his father Kongshou; his mother was née Wang 汪. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hong 洪 and Luo, and his wife was née Qiu. He placed fifty-third in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Xiang, courtesy name Tingpei, was from Yuanwu County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, and belonged to a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged thirty-nine, born on the eleventh day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wang; his grandfather Zhi was granted the title of Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and his father Duo was Left Administration Vice Commissioner. His father's former wives were née Liang, posthumously granted the title Lady of Suitability, and née Zhao; his mother was née Sun, granted the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother was née Bai. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gui, an Instructor of Medicine; Qi; Zan, a tribute scholar; Xuan; and Lian. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighteenth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 219th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tan Pu, courtesy name Dezhou, was from Tongliang County, Hezhou Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, and belonged to a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Zugui, and his father Jin, an Instructor; his mother was née Xiong. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Bo and Yuan, and his wife was née Dong. He placed forty-first in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Lü Xian, registered in Zhending County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Bangyou. First in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Er; his grandfather was Zhong; his father was Liang, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Neng and Jie, and his wife was née Li. He placed 127th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Kai, registered in Xin’an County, Anzhou, Baoding Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Chenghua. Third in birth order, he was twenty-one years old and was born on the fifteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather was Cang, a Police Chief posthumously granted the title of Secretary; his father was Zhao, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; and his mother was née Li, granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Yue and Fu, and his wife was née Li. He placed 50th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 110th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Xu, registered in Xiushui County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiming. Fifth in birth order, he was twenty-three years old and was born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zheng, honored as a Righteous Commoner; his grandfather was Jimin; his father was Song; and his mother was née Zhang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Xun, Xi, Ye, and Xu [?—the same name as the candidate], a county school student; his younger brothers were Can, Ru, Yan, Feng, Li, Wei, and Lian. His wife was née Mei. He placed 52nd in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 49th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Luan, registered in Anqiu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingzhi. Third in birth order, he was twenty-six years old and was born on the eighteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanming; his grandfather was Zeng, an honorary official; his father was Lian, also an honorary official; and his mother was née Wang. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Peng, an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang; his younger brothers were Feng, E, Kun, and Hong. His wife was née Wang. He placed eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jia Guan 賈瓘 was registered in Ningzhou, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the prefectural school of Ningzhou, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Boyu, and he ranked fifth among his brothers. He was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Zhou, his grandfather De, and his father Rang, Commissioner of a Transport Office; his mother was née Mu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cong 琮, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Cong 璁, an honorary official; Rong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and Huang. His younger brother Zhen was a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Zhu. He placed third in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xu 王序 was registered in Pingshan County, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a military household. A county-school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tianzhi, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was thirty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Renmei, his grandfather Rang, and his father Zhang, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of State Ceremonial; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Qing and Bing. His wife was née Cao. He placed sixty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 282nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 弘治三年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟天子
父天母地而為之
子凡天下之民皆
同胞一氣靡所不
統故又曰大君者
===
吾父母宗子宗子
繼承父母君主天
下其責甚大必養
之有道教之有方
舉天下之民無一

punctuated: 皇帝制曰：朕惟天子，父天母地而為之子，凡天下之民，皆同胞一氣，靡所不統。故又曰：「大君者，吾父母宗子。」宗子繼承父母，君主天下，其責甚大。必養之有道，教之有方，舉天下之民，無一
translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: I consider that the Son of Heaven takes Heaven as his father and Earth as his mother and is their son. All the people under Heaven are siblings sharing one vital breath, and none lies outside his governance. Thus it is also said: “The great sovereign is the principal heir of our father and mother.” The principal heir succeeds his father and mother and rules all under Heaven; his responsibility is exceedingly great. He must nourish the people according to the proper Way and instruct them by appropriate methods, so that among all the people under Heaven, not a single one …

title: 弘治三年進士登科錄
text:
考而論之歟夫自
唐虞而下諸君宗
子之責無不同當
時制度之立政令
之行又無不同而
===
要其治效之所至
乃有不能同者此
固世道之漸降然
夷考其實亦尚有
可言歟前賢論儒

From the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun onward, the rulers’ responsibilities as heads of the ancestral lineage were all the same, as were the establishment of institutions and the implementation of governmental commands in their respective times. punctuated: 者之道，每以位天地、育萬物、參天地、贊化育為極至。於是，宗子之責有相關歟？朕膺天命，嗣守祖宗鴻基，宵旰孳孳，思盡宗子之責，比隆古之聖帝明王，其行之之序自何
translation_en: …the Way of scholars, always taking as its highest attainment setting Heaven and Earth in their proper places, nourishing the myriad things, forming a triad with Heaven and Earth, and assisting their transforming and nurturing work. Is the responsibility of the head of the ancestral lineage connected with this? I have received Heaven’s mandate and inherited the duty of preserving the vast foundation established by my ancestors. Rising before dawn and eating late, I labor diligently, seeking to fulfill the responsibility of the head of the ancestral lineage and to equal the greatness of the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity. In what order should this be put into practice, and where should it begin…

title: 弘治三年進士登科錄
text:
臣錢福
臣對臣聞人君盡代天之責以成配天之治者皆一
心之用也蓋心者天之所以與我者也天下者天之
所以責我者也天不能自養乎民而責我以養天不
能自教乎民而責我以教所以與我者與人同而所
以責乎我者獨備故凡所以教養乎天下者必反而
求之乎心天下雖大一心運之而有餘矣苟不求之
天之所以與我之心而徒務乎責我者之事則為之
而不得其本施之而不得其序養民雖勤而終非仁
心實惠之寓教民雖悉而終非躬行心得之推欲天
===
下民物之各得其所亦難矣天下之有一不得其所
則天之所以責我者不能盡是天地自天地民物自
民物而吾身自吾身尚得為天地之宗子乎哉天如
此其高地如此其厚而吾之治如此其小尚得為配
天之治乎哉書曰天佑下民作之君作之師惟其克
相上帝寵綏四方易曰后以財成天地之道輔相天
地之宜以左右民皆言人君受天與之全任天責之
重必當盡是責以成是治也然要其所以為之者豈
出於一心之外哉即是而觀則唐堯虞舜夏禹商湯
周武之底於盛治漢唐宋之僅為小康與

臣錢福。
臣對：臣聞，人君盡代天之責，以成配天之治者，皆一心之用也。蓋心者，天之所以與我者也；天下者，天之所以責我者也。天不能自養乎民，而責我以養；天不能自教乎民，而責我以教。所以與我者與人同，而所以責乎我者獨備。故凡所以教養乎天下者，必反而求之乎心。天下雖大，一心運之而有餘矣。苟不求之天之所以與我之心，而徒務乎責我者之事，則為之而不得其本，施之而不得其序。養民雖勤，而終非仁心實惠之寓；教民雖悉，而終非躬行心得之推。欲天下民物之各得其所，亦難矣。天下之有一不得其所，則天之所以責我者不能盡。是天地自天地，民物自民物，而吾身自吾身，尚得為天地之宗子乎哉？天如此其高，地如此其厚，而吾之治如此其小，尚得為配天之治乎哉？《書》曰：「天佑下民，作之君，作之師，惟其克相上帝，寵綏四方。」《易》曰：「后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」皆言人君受天與之全，任天責之重，必當盡是責，以成是治也。然要其所以為之者，豈出於一心之外哉？即是而觀，則唐堯、虞舜、夏禹、商湯、周武之底於盛治，漢、唐、宋之僅為小康，與
translation_en:
Your servant Qian Fu.

Your servant replies: I have heard that when a ruler fulfills his responsibility to act on Heaven’s behalf and achieves a government worthy of matching Heaven, it is entirely through the workings of his single heart. For the heart is what Heaven has bestowed upon me; all under Heaven is what Heaven has entrusted to my care. Heaven cannot itself nourish the people, so it charges me with nourishing them; Heaven cannot itself teach the people, so it charges me with teaching them. What Heaven has bestowed upon me is the same as what it bestows upon others, but the responsibilities it places upon me alone are comprehensive. Thus, in everything by which one teaches and nourishes all under Heaven, one must turn back and seek the source within the heart. Vast though all under Heaven may be, a single heart has more than enough capacity to guide it.

If, instead of seeking within the heart that Heaven has bestowed upon me, I merely busy myself with the affairs entrusted to me, then my actions will lack their foundation and their execution will lack the proper sequence. Though diligent in nourishing the people, I will ultimately fail to embody a benevolent heart in tangible benefits; though thorough in teaching them, I will ultimately fail to extend to them what I have personally practiced and inwardly understood. It will then be difficult to ensure that all people and things under Heaven find their proper place. If even one fails to find its proper place, I have not fully discharged the responsibility Heaven has entrusted to me. In that case, Heaven and Earth remain apart, people and things remain apart, and I myself remain apart. Could I still be the principal heir of Heaven and Earth? Heaven is so high, Earth so deep, yet my government is so petty: could it still be a government worthy of matching Heaven?

The Book of Documents says: “Heaven aids the people below, appointing rulers and teachers for them, that they may assist the Lord on High and cherish and pacify the four quarters.” The Book of Changes says: “The sovereign shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby guides the people.” Both passages say that the ruler receives in full what Heaven bestows and bears the weighty responsibilities Heaven entrusts to him; he must fully discharge those responsibilities to achieve such government. Yet, as to the essential means of doing so, could these lie anywhere beyond his single heart? Viewed in this light, the attainment of flourishing government by Yao of Tang, Shun of Yu, Yu of Xia, Tang of Shang, and Wu of Zhou, the attainment of only modest peace and prosperity by the Han, Tang, and Song, and …

title: 弘治三年進士登科錄
text:
今日之欲比隆前古者蓋必有說矣洪惟
皇帝陛下鍾天地之粹氣禀天地之全德以撫有普天率
土之人民
臨御以来勵精圖治凡可以當天心慰人望者無所不
用其極誠可謂大有為之
君可謂善繼述之
宗子矣然乃不自滿足首進臣等於
廷詢之以父母宗子之責且謂儒者之道以位天地育
萬物參天地賛化育為極至而求行之之序所自始
焉臣有以見
===
陛下之心真知儒道之至重深圖君責之惟艱直欲無一
念之愧乎天無一事之愧乎古無一制度無一政令
之不得其宜無一民一物之不被其澤而後已顧臣
愚昧何足以知之然於乾坤之間得與胞與之列厠
名為儒久荷
教育竊有志乎聖賢之學其於參賛之功冢相之事雖
不敢與聞而所得於天以生之理為心之所固有者
固不容諉於不知矣敢不援經擿史為
陛下陳之臣惟天子父天母地而為之子云者此漢儒班
固之言也大君者吾父母宗子云者此宋儒張載之

名為儒久荷
